title: Notation
body_md:
We use $\mathbb{N}$ for the type of natural numbers at the meta-level.
Contexts are snoc-lists written $\Gamma, x : T$.
Application of a substitution $\sigma$ to a term $t$ is written $t[\sigma]$, and
composition of substitutions is written $\sigma \circ \tau$ (meaning first $\sigma$, then $\tau$).

title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:raw-exp}
  The set $\textsf{Exp}$ of raw expressions is generated by the following grammar:
  \[
    \begin{array}{rcll}
      t, s, S, T \in \textsf{Exp} & ::= & x & \text{(variable)} \\
                          & \mid & \ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}} & \text{(universe at level $i$)} \\
                          & \mid & \ensuremath{\texttt{Nat}} & \text{(natural number type)} \\
                          & \mid & \Pi(x : S).\, T & \text{(dependent function type, $x$ bound in $T$)} \\
                          & \mid & \textsf{zero} & \text{(zero)} \\
                          & \mid & \textsf{succ}~t & \text{(successor)} \\
                          & \mid & \ensuremath{\textsf{elim}_{\ensuremath{\texttt{Nat}}}~(x.\,T)~z~(x, y.\, s)~t} & \text{(natural number eliminator)} \\
                          & \mid & \lambda x.\, t & \text{(lambda abstraction, $x$ bound in $t$)} \\
                          & \mid & r~s & \text{(application)}
    \end{array}
  \]

\label{def:ctx}
  Contexts $\Gamma, \Delta \in \textsf{Ctx}$ are ordered lists of variable-type pairs:
  \[
    \Gamma \in \textsf{Ctx} \quad ::= \quad \cdot \quad \mid \quad \Gamma, x : S
  \]
  where $\cdot$ is the empty context and $\Gamma, x : S$ extends $\Gamma$ with a fresh
  variable $x$ of type $S \in \textsf{Exp}$.
  We write $|\Gamma|$ for the length of $\Gamma$.

title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:wk}
  A \emph{weakening} is a function $\phi : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$.
  The key operations on weakenings are:
  \begin{align*}
    \ensuremath{\textsf{id}} &: \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N} & \ensuremath{\textsf{id}}(x) &= x \\
    {\Uparrow} &: \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N} & {\Uparrow}(x) &= x + 1 \\
    q(\phi) &: \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N} & q(\phi)(0) &= 0 \\
    && q(\phi)(x+1) &= \phi(x) + 1
  \end{align*}
  The shift $\Uparrow$ increments all indices by one (corresponding to introducing one new
  binding).
  The operation $q(\phi)$ extends a weakening under a binder: it fixes index~$0$
  (the newly bound variable) and applies $\phi$ followed by a successor to all
  other indices.
head: environment
name: Weakenings

title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:wk-app}
  The application of a weakening $\phi$ to a term $t$, written $t[\phi]$, is
  defined by recursion on the structure of $t$:
  \begin{align*}
    x[\phi] &= \phi(x) \\
    \ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}[\phi] &= \ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}} \\
    \ensuremath{\texttt{Nat}}[\phi] &= \ensuremath{\texttt{Nat}} \\
    (\Pi(x : S).\, T)[\phi] &= \Pi(x : S[\phi]).\, (T[q(\phi)]) \\
    \textsf{zero}[\phi] &= \textsf{zero} \\
    (\textsf{succ}~t)[\phi] &= \textsf{succ}~(t[\phi]) \\
    (\ensuremath{\textsf{elim}_{\ensuremath{\texttt{Nat}}}~(x.\,T)~z~(x, y.\, s)~t})[\phi] &= \ensuremath{\textsf{elim}_{\ensuremath{\texttt{Nat}}}~(x.\,T[q(\phi)])~z[\phi]~(x,y.\, s[q^2(\phi)])~t[\phi]} \\
    (\lambda x.\, t)[\phi] &= \lambda x.\, t[q(\phi)] \\
    (r\; s)[\phi] &= (r[\phi])\; (s[\phi])
  \end{align*}
  Whenever we pass under a binder, we extend the weakening with $q$.
  The successor case of the eliminator binds two variables ($x$ for the predecessor,
  $y$ for the inductive hypothesis), hence $q$ is applied twice.

title: Proof
body_md:
By induction on $t$.
  We show a few representative cases.
  \begin{itemize}[label=Case]
  \@idxitem $t = x$ (variable).
    \begin{align*}
      x[\phi][\psi] = (\phi(x))[\psi] = \psi(\phi(x)) = (\phi \circ \psi)(x) = x[\phi \circ \psi]

  \@idxitem $t = \lambda x.\, t'$.
    \begin{align*}
      (\lambda x.\, t')[\phi][\psi]
      &= (\lambda x.\, (t'[q(\phi)]))[\psi] \\
      &= \lambda x.\, (t'[q(\phi)][q(\psi)]) \\
      &= \lambda x.\, (t'[q(\phi) \circ q(\psi)])
        \tag{by IH} \\
      &= \lambda x.\, (t'[q(\phi \circ \psi)])
        \tag{by \Cref{lem:wk-q-comp}} \\
      &= (\lambda x.\, t')[\phi \circ \psi]
    \end{align*}
  \@idxitem $t = \ensuremath{\textsf{elim}_{\ensuremath{\texttt{Nat}}}~(x.\,T)~z~(x, y.\, s)~t'}$.
    \begin{align*}
      & (\ensuremath{\textsf{elim}_{\ensuremath{\texttt{Nat}}}~(x.\,T)~z~(x, y.\, s)~t'})[\phi][\psi] \\
      &= (\ensuremath{\textsf{elim}_{\ensuremath{\texttt{Nat}}}~(x.\,T[q(\phi)])~z[\phi]~(x, y.\, s[q^2(\phi)])~t'[\phi]})[\psi] \\
      &= \ensuremath{\textsf{elim}_{\ensuremath{\texttt{Nat}}}~(x.\,T[q(\phi)][q(\psi)])~z[\phi][\psi]~(x, y.\, s[q^2(\phi)][q^2(\psi)])~t'[\phi][\psi]} \\
      &= \ensuremath{\textsf{elim}_{\ensuremath{\texttt{Nat}}}~(x.\,T[q(\phi) \circ q(\psi)])~z[\phi \circ \psi]~(x, y.\, s[q^2(\phi) \circ q^2(\psi)])~t'[\phi \circ \psi]}
        \tag{by IH} \\
      &= \ensuremath{\textsf{elim}_{\ensuremath{\texttt{Nat}}}~(x.\,T[q(\phi \circ \psi)])~z[\phi \circ \psi]~(x, y.\, s[q^2(\phi \circ \psi)])~t'[\phi \circ \psi]}
        \tag{by \Cref{lem:wk-qn-comp}} \\
      &= (\ensuremath{\textsf{elim}_{\ensuremath{\texttt{Nat}}}~(x.\,T)~z~(x, y.\, s)~t'})[\phi \circ \psi]
    \end{align*}
  \end{itemize}
  The cases for $\textsf{succ}~t$, $r\; s$, $\Pi$, $\ensuremath{\texttt{Nat}}$, $\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}$, and $\textsf{zero}$ are similar or
  immediate.

title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:subst-ops}
  We define the following operations on substitutions:
  \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
    \@idxitem \textbf{Identity.}
      $\ensuremath{\textsf{id}} : \textsf{Subst}$, defined by $\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}(x) = x$.
    \@idxitem \textbf{Extension (cons).}
      Given a substitution $\sigma$, a variable $x$, and a term $s$, we write
      $(\sigma, s/x)$ for the substitution:
      \[
        (\sigma, s/x)(0) = s \qquad (\sigma, s/x)(x+1) = \sigma(x)
      \]
      Here $x$ is a visual mnemonic for the variable at de Bruijn index~0;
      under the hood, the extension always targets index~0.
    \@idxitem \textbf{Lifting under a binder.}
      Given a substitution $\sigma$, we define $q(\sigma) : \textsf{Subst}$ by:
      \[
        q(\sigma)(0) = 0 \qquad q(\sigma)(x+1) = (\sigma(x))[\Uparrow]
      \]
      This fixes index~0 and applies $\sigma$ to the remaining indices, weakening the
      results by one to account for the new binder.
    \@idxitem \textbf{Applying a weakening to a substitution.}
      Given a substitution $\sigma$ and a weakening $\phi$, we define
      $\sigma[\phi] : \textsf{Subst}$ pointwise:
      \[
        (\sigma[\phi])(x) = (\sigma(x))[\phi]
      \]
    \@idxitem \textbf{Composition.}
      Given substitutions $\sigma$ and $\tau$, their composition is:
      \[
        (\sigma \circ \tau)(x) = (\sigma(x))[\tau]
      \]
  \end{enumerate}

title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:wk-embed}
  Every weakening $\phi$ can be regarded as a substitution via the embedding:
  \[
    \iota(\phi) : \textsf{Subst} \qquad \iota(\phi)(x) = \phi(x)
  \]
  That is, $\iota(\phi)$ maps each index $n$ to the variable $\phi(x)$.
head: environment
name: Embedding of Weakenings into Substitutions

title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Embedding Correctness

title: Proof
body_md:
By induction on $t$.
  The key observation is that $q(\iota(\phi)) = \iota(q(\phi))$:
  \begin{align*}
    q(\iota(\phi))(0) &= 0 = \iota(q(\phi))(0) \\
    q(\iota(\phi))(x+1) &= \iota(\phi)(x)[\Uparrow] = \phi(x)[\Uparrow] = \phi(x) + 1 = \iota(q(\phi))(x+1)
  \end{align*}
  With this fact, the induction is straightforward: at each binding form, we use
  $q(\iota(\phi)) = \iota(q(\phi))$ to relate the substitution side to the weakening side.
  For example:
  \begin{align*}
    (\lambda x.\, t')[\iota(\phi)]
    &= \lambda x.\, (t'[q(\iota(\phi))]) \\
    &= \lambda x.\, (t'[\iota(q(\phi))]) \\
    &= \lambda x.\, (t'[q(\phi)])
      \tag{by IH} \\
    &= (\lambda x.\, t')[\phi]
  \end{align*}

title: Proof
body_md:

  \@idxitem $\iota(\Uparrow)(x) = \Uparrow(x) = x + 1$.
    As a substitution, this is the variable $x+1$, which equals $\Uparrow$ viewed as a substitution.
  \@idxitem Already shown in the proof of \Cref{lem:wk-embed-correct}:
    $q(\iota(\phi))(0) = 0 = \iota(q(\phi))(0)$ and

      &= \psi(\phi(x))

      &= (\phi \circ \psi)(x) \\
      &= \iota(\phi \circ \psi)(x)

      &= \lambda x.\, t'

    \begin{align*}
      (\Pi(x:S).\, T)[\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}]
      &= \Pi(x : S[\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}]).\, (T[q(\ensuremath{\textsf{id}})]) \\
      &= \Pi(x : S).\, (T[\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}])
        \tag{by IH and \Cref{lem:subst-q-id}} \\
      &= \Pi(x : S).\, T
        \tag{by IH}
    \end{align*}

title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Action of $q^n$ on Indices

title: Proof
body_md:
By induction on $n$.
  \begin{itemize}[label=Case]
  \@idxitem $n = 0$: (1) vacuous. (2) $q^0(\phi)(0) = \phi(0) = \phi(0) + 0$.
    (3) $q^0(\phi)(x) = \phi(x) = \phi(x - 0) + 0$.
  \@idxitem $n + 1$: We use $q^{n+1}(\phi) = q(q^n(\phi))$.
    \begin{enumerate}
    \@idxitem If $x < n+1$: either $x = 0$ (then $q(q^n(\phi))(0) = 0 = x$) or
      $x = y + 1$ with $y < n$ (then $q(q^n(\phi))(y+1) = q^n(\phi)(y) + 1 = y + 1 = x$
      by the IH).
    \@idxitem $x = n + 1$: $q(q^n(\phi))(n+1) = q^n(\phi)(n) + 1 = (\phi(0) + n) + 1 = \phi(0) + (n+1)$
      by the IH.
    \@idxitem $x > n + 1$: $x = y + 1$ with $y > n$.
      $q(q^n(\phi))(y+1) = q^n(\phi)(y) + 1 = (\phi(y - n) + n) + 1 = \phi((y+1) - (n+1)) + (n+1)$
      by the IH.
    \end{enumerate}
  \end{itemize}

title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Action of $q^n$ on Substitution Indices

title: Proof
body_md:
By induction on $n$.
  \begin{itemize}[label=Case]
  \@idxitem $n = 0$: (1) vacuous. (2) $q^0(\sigma)(0) = \sigma(0) = \sigma(0)[\Uparrow^0]$.
    (3) $q^0(\sigma)(x) = \sigma(x) = \sigma(x-0)[\Uparrow^0]$.
  \@idxitem $n + 1$: We use $q^{n+1}(\sigma) = q(q^n(\sigma))$.
    \begin{enumerate}
    \@idxitem If $x < n+1$: either $x = 0$ (then $q(q^n(\sigma))(0) = 0 = x$) or
      $x = y + 1$ with $y < n$ (then $q(q^n(\sigma))(y+1) = (q^n(\sigma)(y))[\Uparrow] = y[\Uparrow] = y + 1 = x$
      by the IH (1)).
    \@idxitem $x = n + 1$:
      \begin{align*}
        q(q^n(\sigma))(n+1) &= (q^n(\sigma)(n))[\Uparrow] \\
        &= (\sigma(0)[\Uparrow^n])[\Uparrow]
          \tag{by IH (2)} \\
        &= \sigma(0)[\Uparrow^{n+1}]
          \tag{by \Cref{lem:wk-comp}}
      \end{align*}
    \@idxitem $x > n+1$: $x = y + 1$ with $y > n$.
      \begin{align*}
        q(q^n(\sigma))(y+1) &= (q^n(\sigma)(y))[\Uparrow] \\
        &= (\sigma(y - n)[\Uparrow^n])[\Uparrow]
          \tag{by IH (3)} \\
        &= \sigma(y - n)[\Uparrow^{n+1}]
          \tag{by \Cref{lem:wk-comp}} \\
        &= \sigma((y+1) - (n+1))[\Uparrow^{n+1}]
      \end{align*}
    \end{enumerate}
  \end{itemize}

      &= ((\sigma \circ \tau)(x))[\Uparrow] \\

title: Proof
body_md:
By \Cref{lem:subst-assoc}, it suffices to show $q(\sigma) \circ (\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}, s/x) = (\sigma, s/x)$.
  Recall $q(\sigma) = (\sigma[\Uparrow], 0/x)$.
  By \Cref{lem:ext-comp}:
  \begin{align*}
    q(\sigma) \circ (\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}, s/x)
    &= (\sigma[\Uparrow], 0/x) \circ (\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}, s/x) \\
    &= (\sigma[\Uparrow] \circ (\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}, s/x),\; 0[(\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}, s/x)]/x)
      \tag{by \Cref{lem:ext-comp}} \\
    &= ((\sigma \circ \Uparrow) \circ (\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}, s/x),\; s/x) \\
    &= (\sigma \circ (\Uparrow \circ (\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}, s/x)),\; s/x)
       \\
    &= (\sigma \circ \ensuremath{\textsf{id}},\; s/x) \tag{by \Cref{lem:shift-ext}} \\
    &= (\sigma, s/x)
      \tag{by \Cref{lem:subst-id}}
  \end{align*}

    q(\sigma) \circ (\phi, s/x)
    &= (\sigma[\Uparrow], 0/x) \circ (\phi, s/x) \\
    &= (\sigma[\Uparrow] \circ (\phi, s/x),\; 0[(\phi, s/x)]/x)
      \tag{by \Cref{lem:ext-comp}} \\
    &= ((\sigma \circ \Uparrow) \circ (\phi, s/x),\; s/x) \\
    &= (\sigma \circ (\Uparrow \circ (\phi, s/x)),\; s/x)
      \tag{by \Cref{lem:subst-cat} associativity} \\
    &= (\sigma \circ \phi,\; s/x)
      \tag{by \Cref{lem:shift-ext}} \\
    &= (\sigma[\phi],\; s/x)
  \end{align*}

title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:q-subst-equiv}
  If $\judge[\Gamma]{\sigma \approx \sigma' : \Delta}$ and

head: environment
name: $q$ Preserves Substitution Equivalence

title: Proof
body_md:
By \Cref{lem:q-subst-typing}, $\judge[\Gamma, x:S[\sigma]]{q(\sigma) :
    (\Delta, x:S)}$. We need $\judge[\Gamma, x:S[\sigma]]{q(\sigma') :
    (\Delta, x:S)}$ as well: from
  $\tyequiv[\Gamma]{S[\sigma]}{S[\sigma']}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}$
  (by \Cref{lem:subst-preserves} statement~(2) applied to
  reflexivity on $\typing[\Delta]{S}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}$), the contexts
  $\Gamma, x:S[\sigma]$ and $\Gamma, x:S[\sigma']$ are equivalent, so
  $\judge[\Gamma, x:S[\sigma]]{q(\sigma') : (\Delta, x:S)}$ by
  \Cref{lem:q-subst-typing} and a context-conversion step.

  We verify clause~(2): for every $y : T \in \Delta, x:S$,
  $\tyequiv[\Gamma, x:S[\sigma]]{q(\sigma)(y)}{q(\sigma')(y)}
  {T[q(\sigma)]}$.
  \begin{itemize}
  \@idxitem $y = x_0$: $T = S[\Uparrow]$, $q(\sigma)(x_0) = x_0 =
    q(\sigma')(x_0)$. The required equality is reflexivity on $x_0$ at
    $S[\Uparrow][q(\sigma)] = S[\sigma][\Uparrow]$ (by
    \Cref{lem:wk-subst-comm}).
  \@idxitem $y = 1{+}z$ where $z : T' \in \Delta$:
    $q(\sigma)(1{+}z) = \sigma(z)[\Uparrow]$ and
    $q(\sigma')(1{+}z) = \sigma'(z)[\Uparrow]$. By clause~(2) of
    \Cref{def:subst-equiv} on $\sigma \approx \sigma'$,
    $\tyequiv[\Gamma]{\sigma(z)}{\sigma'(z)}{T'[\sigma]}$. By
    \Cref{lem:wk-typing} applied to $\Uparrow$,
    $\tyequiv[\Gamma, x:S[\sigma]]
      {\sigma(z)[\Uparrow]}{\sigma'(z)[\Uparrow]}
      {T'[\sigma][\Uparrow]}$,
    and $T'[\sigma][\Uparrow] = T'[\Uparrow][q(\sigma)]$ by
    \Cref{lem:wk-subst-comm}, which equals $T[q(\sigma)]$.
  \end{itemize}

head: environment
name: Base PERs are PERs

title: Proof
body_md:
Symmetry is immediate (swap the two conjuncts).
  Transitivity follows from determinism of readback (\Cref{lem:det}).

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case} $\textsf{Ne}$.
  Suppose $e \approx e' \in \textsf{Ne}$ and $e' \approx e'' \in \textsf{Ne}$.
  \begin{align*}
    &\forall\, n.\; \exists\, u.\;
      \textsf{R}^{\textsf{Ne}}_n(e) \searrow u \;\wedge\; \textsf{R}^{\textsf{Ne}}_n(e') \searrow u
      && \text{(by first hypothesis)} \\
    &\forall\, n.\; \exists\, u'.\;
      \textsf{R}^{\textsf{Ne}}_n(e') \searrow u' \;\wedge\; \textsf{R}^{\textsf{Ne}}_n(e'') \searrow u'
      && \text{(by second hypothesis)} \\
    &u = u'
      && \text{(by determinism of $\textsf{R}^{\textsf{Ne}}$, \Cref{lem:det})} \\
    &\textsf{R}^{\textsf{Ne}}_n(e) \searrow u \;\wedge\; \textsf{R}^{\textsf{Ne}}_n(e'') \searrow u
      && \text{(combining above)}
  \end{align*}

  \medskip\noindent
  The cases for $\textsf{Nf}$ and $\textsf{Ty}$ are analogous, using determinism of
  $\textsf{R}^{\textsf{Nf}}$ and $\textsf{R}^{\textsf{Ty}}$ respectively.

title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Semantic weakening gives semantic substitution

title: Proof
body_md:
We must show: for all $\Gamma' \approx \Gamma' \searrow R'$, all
  $\semweak[\Gamma']{\phi}{\Delta}$, and all $\rho \approx \rho' \in R'$,
  \[
    \{\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi[\phi] \rrbracket(\rho)},\; \ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \phi \rrbracket(\rho)})},\;
    \ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \phi \rrbracket(\rho')})},\; \ensuremath{\llbracket \psi[\phi] \rrbracket(\rho')}\} \subseteq R_\Gamma.
  \]

  Recall from \Cref{sec:sem} that the evaluation of a weakening $\psi$ in an
  environment $\rho$ is defined by $\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho)}(n) = \rho(\psi(n))$, i.e.,
  it reindexes the environment according to $\psi$.
  We compute each of the four values:
  \begin{align*}
    &\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi[\phi] \rrbracket(\rho)}
      = \ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \circ \phi \rrbracket(\rho)}
      && \text{(since $\psi[\phi] = \psi \circ \phi$ for weakenings)} \\
    &\quad = \lambda n.\, \rho((\psi \circ \phi)(n))
      = \lambda n.\, \rho(\phi(\psi(n)))
      && \text{(by definition of weakening evaluation)} \\[4pt]
    &\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \phi \rrbracket(\rho)})}
      = \lambda n.\, (\ensuremath{\llbracket \phi \rrbracket(\rho)})(\psi(n))
      && \text{(by definition of weakening evaluation)} \\
    &\quad = \lambda n.\, \rho(\phi(\psi(n)))
      && \text{(since $\ensuremath{\llbracket \phi \rrbracket(\rho)}(k) = \rho(\phi(k))$)}
  \end{align*}
  Hence $\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi[\phi] \rrbracket(\rho)} = \ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \phi \rrbracket(\rho)})}$ --- the commutation
  is definitional for weakenings.
  Similarly $\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi[\phi] \rrbracket(\rho')} = \ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \phi \rrbracket(\rho')})}$.
  So all four values collapse to two:
  \[
    \ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \circ \phi \rrbracket(\rho)} \quad\text{and}\quad \ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \circ \phi \rrbracket(\rho')}.
  \]
  From $\semweak[\Gamma']{\phi}{\Delta}$ and $\rho \approx \rho' \in R'$, we have
  $\ensuremath{\llbracket \phi \rrbracket(\rho)} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket \phi \rrbracket(\rho')} \in R_\Delta$.
  From $\semweak[\Delta]{\psi}{\Gamma}$ and
  $\ensuremath{\llbracket \phi \rrbracket(\rho)} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket \phi \rrbracket(\rho')} \in R_\Delta$, we have
  \begin{align*}
    &\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \phi \rrbracket(\rho)})} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \phi \rrbracket(\rho')})} \in R_\Gamma
      && \text{(by the definition of $\semweak[\Delta]{\psi}{\Gamma}$)}
  \end{align*}
  Since all four values equal $\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \circ \phi \rrbracket(\rho)}$ or
  $\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \circ \phi \rrbracket(\rho')}$ (which equal the inner two by the above computation),
  the four-way relatedness follows by symmetry (\Cref{lem:ctx-sym}) and
  transitivity (\Cref{lem:ctx-trans}) of $R_\Gamma$.

\label{lem:sem-wk-subst}

head: environment
name: Precomposition with weakening

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\Gamma' \approx \Gamma' \searrow R'$ be given, with
  $\semweak[\Gamma']{\phi}{\Gamma}$ and $\rho \approx \rho' \in R'$.
  We must show:
  \[
    \{\ensuremath{\llbracket (\sigma[\psi])[\phi] \rrbracket(\rho)},\; \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma[\psi] \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \phi \rrbracket(\rho)})},\;
    \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma'[\psi] \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \phi \rrbracket(\rho')})},\; \ensuremath{\llbracket (\sigma'[\psi])[\phi] \rrbracket(\rho')}\}
    \subseteq R_{\Delta'}.
  \]

  We make two instantiations of the hypothesis $\semtyeq[\Delta]{\sigma}{\sigma'}{\Delta'}$.

  \emph{First instantiation}: at $\Gamma'$, the composed semantic weakening
  $\semweak[\Gamma']{\psi \circ \phi}{\Delta}$
  (by \Cref{lem:sem-wk-comp} from $\semweak[\Gamma']{\phi}{\Gamma}$ and
  $\semweak[\Gamma]{\psi}{\Delta}$), and $\rho \approx \rho' \in R'$:
  \[
    \{\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma[\psi \circ \phi] \rrbracket(\rho)},\;
    \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \circ \phi \rrbracket(\rho)})},\;
    \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma' \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \circ \phi \rrbracket(\rho')})},\;
    \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma'[\psi \circ \phi] \rrbracket(\rho')}\} \subseteq R_{\Delta'}.
  \]
  Since $(\sigma[\psi])[\phi] = \sigma[\psi \circ \phi]$ (by \Cref{lem:wk-subst-comm}),
  the outer values are $\ensuremath{\llbracket (\sigma[\psi])[\phi] \rrbracket(\rho)}$ and $\ensuremath{\llbracket (\sigma'[\psi])[\phi] \rrbracket(\rho')}$.

  \emph{Second instantiation}: at $\Gamma$ with $R_\Gamma$, the semantic weakening
  $\semweak[\Gamma]{\psi}{\Delta}$ (given), and
  $\ensuremath{\llbracket \phi \rrbracket(\rho)} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket \phi \rrbracket(\rho')} \in R_\Gamma$
  (from $\semweak[\Gamma']{\phi}{\Gamma}$ applied to $\rho \approx \rho' \in R'$):
  \[
    \{\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma[\psi] \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \phi \rrbracket(\rho)})},\;
    \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \phi \rrbracket(\rho)})})},\;
    \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma' \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \phi \rrbracket(\rho')})})},\;
    \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma'[\psi] \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \phi \rrbracket(\rho')})}\} \subseteq R_{\Delta'}.
  \]
  The outer values here are $\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma[\psi] \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \phi \rrbracket(\rho)})}$ and
  $\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma'[\psi] \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \phi \rrbracket(\rho')})}$ --- exactly the inner values of our goal.

  Now observe: since $\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \circ \phi \rrbracket(\rho)} = \ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \phi \rrbracket(\rho)})}$
  (weakenings commute with evaluation definitionally), the inner values of both
  instantiations coincide:
  $\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \circ \phi \rrbracket(\rho)})} = \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \phi \rrbracket(\rho)})})}$.

  From the first instantiation:
  $\ensuremath{\llbracket (\sigma[\psi])[\phi] \rrbracket(\rho)} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \phi \rrbracket(\rho)})})} \in R_{\Delta'}$.
  From the second instantiation:
  $\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma[\psi] \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \phi \rrbracket(\rho)})} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \phi \rrbracket(\rho)})})} \in R_{\Delta'}$.
  By symmetry and transitivity of $R_{\Delta'}$, all four goal values are related:
  \begin{align*}
    &\ensuremath{\llbracket (\sigma[\psi])[\phi] \rrbracket(\rho)} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma[\psi] \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \phi \rrbracket(\rho)})} \in R_{\Delta'}
      && \text{(by transitivity through the shared inner value)} \\
    &\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma'[\psi] \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \phi \rrbracket(\rho')})} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket (\sigma'[\psi])[\phi] \rrbracket(\rho')} \in R_{\Delta'}
      && \text{(similarly for the primed side)} \\
    &\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma[\psi] \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \phi \rrbracket(\rho)})} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma'[\psi] \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \phi \rrbracket(\rho')})} \in R_{\Delta'}
      && \text{(from the second instantiation, outer-left $\approx$ outer-right)}
  \end{align*}
  Hence $\{\ensuremath{\llbracket (\sigma[\psi])[\phi] \rrbracket(\rho)},\; \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma[\psi] \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \phi \rrbracket(\rho)})},\;
  \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma'[\psi] \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \phi \rrbracket(\rho')})},\; \ensuremath{\llbracket (\sigma'[\psi])[\phi] \rrbracket(\rho')}\} \subseteq R_{\Delta'}$.

title: Proof
body_md:

  From the hypothesis $\semtyeq[\Gamma]{\sigma}{\sigma'}{\Delta}$ applied at
  $\Gamma'$, $\psi$, and $\rho' \approx \rho \in R'$
  (using symmetry of $R'$, \Cref{lem:ctx-sym}):
  \[
    \{\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma[\psi] \rrbracket(\rho')},\; \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho')})},\;

  This gives us $\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma[\psi] \rrbracket(\rho')} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho')})} \in R_\Delta$
  and $\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma' \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho)})} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma'[\psi] \rrbracket(\rho)} \in R_\Delta$.

  By symmetry of $R_\Delta$ (\Cref{lem:ctx-sym}), we can reverse pairs.
  The four values $\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma'[\psi] \rrbracket(\rho)}$, $\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma' \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho)})}$,

  relatedness.

name: Transitivity of semantic substitutions

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\Gamma' \approx \Gamma' \searrow R'$, $\semweak[\Gamma']{\psi}{\Gamma}$,
  and $\rho \approx \rho' \in R'$ be given.
  From the first hypothesis:
  \[
    \{\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma[\psi] \rrbracket(\rho)},\; \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho)})},\;
    \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma' \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho')})},\; \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma'[\psi] \rrbracket(\rho')}\} \subseteq R_\Delta.
  \]
  In particular, $\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho)})} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma' \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho')})} \in R_\Delta$.

  From the second hypothesis applied at the same $\Gamma'$, $\psi$, and $\rho \approx \rho'$:
  \[
    \{\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma'[\psi] \rrbracket(\rho)},\; \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma' \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho)})},\;
    \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma'' \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho')})},\; \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma''[\psi] \rrbracket(\rho')}\} \subseteq R_\Delta.
  \]
  In particular, $\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma' \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho)})} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma'' \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho')})} \in R_\Delta$.

  By transitivity of $R_\Delta$ (\Cref{lem:ctx-trans}), using
  $\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho)})} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma' \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho')})} \in R_\Delta$
  and (after mediating through symmetry)
  $\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma' \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho')})} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma'' \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho')})} \in R_\Delta$,
  we get $\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho)})} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma'' \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho')})} \in R_\Delta$.

  For the outer pair: by similar reasoning on the weakened substitutions,
  $\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma[\psi] \rrbracket(\rho)} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho)})} \in R_\Delta$
  (from the first hypothesis) and
  $\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma'' \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho')})} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma''[\psi] \rrbracket(\rho')} \in R_\Delta$
  (from the second hypothesis).
  By transitivity, all four values are related in $R_\Delta$:
  \[
    \{\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma[\psi] \rrbracket(\rho)},\; \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho)})},\;
    \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma'' \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho')})},\; \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma''[\psi] \rrbracket(\rho')}\} \subseteq R_\Delta.
    \qedhere
  \]

title: Proof
body_md:
From $\semweak[\Gamma]{\psi}{\Delta}$ we have
  $\Gamma \approx \Gamma \searrow R_\Gamma$ and
  $\Delta \approx \Delta \searrow R_\Delta$.
  By \Cref{lem:sem-ty-id} on $\semtyeq[\Delta]{S}{S}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}$: for every
  $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_\Delta :: \rho_0 \approx \rho_0' \in R_\Delta$, there is $R_H^\Delta(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_\Delta)$
  with $\ensuremath{\llbracket S \rrbracket(\rho_0)} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket S \rrbracket(\rho_0')} \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_H^\Delta(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_\Delta)$.
  By \textsc{Ctx-Ext}, this gives
  $(\Delta, x:S) \approx (\Delta, x:S) \searrow R_{\Delta,S}$.

  By \Cref{lem:sem-wk}, $\psi$ gives $\semtyeq[\Gamma]{\psi}{\psi}{\Delta}$.
  Applying $\semtyeq[\Delta]{S}{S}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}$ at $\Gamma$ with this semantic
  substitution and any $\rho_0 \approx \rho_0' \in R_\Gamma$, the type part gives
  in particular
  $\ensuremath{\llbracket S[\psi] \rrbracket(\rho_0)} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket S \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho_0)})} \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_H^\Gamma$
  (commutation).
  By \textsc{Ctx-Ext}, this yields
  $(\Gamma, x:S[\psi]) \approx (\Gamma, x:S[\psi]) \searrow R_{\Gamma,S[\psi]}$.

  We must show: for all $\rho \approx \rho' \in R_{\Gamma, S[\psi]}$,
  $\ensuremath{\llbracket q(\psi) \rrbracket(\rho)} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket q(\psi) \rrbracket(\rho')} \in R_{\Delta, S}$.
  By the biconditional of $R_{\Delta, S}$, we must exhibit evidence
  $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}} :: (\ensuremath{\llbracket q(\psi) \rrbracket(\rho)})[\Uparrow] \approx (\ensuremath{\llbracket q(\psi) \rrbracket(\rho')})[\Uparrow] \in R_\Delta$
  with $(\ensuremath{\llbracket q(\psi) \rrbracket(\rho)})(0) \approx (\ensuremath{\llbracket q(\psi) \rrbracket(\rho')})(0) \in R_H^\Delta(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}})$.

  \emph{Tail.}
  \begin{align*}
    &(\ensuremath{\llbracket q(\psi) \rrbracket(\rho)})[\Uparrow] = \ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho[\Uparrow])}
      && \text{(since $(\ensuremath{\llbracket q(\psi) \rrbracket(\rho)})[\Uparrow](n) = \rho(q(\psi)(n{+}1)) = \rho(\psi(n){+}1) = \rho[\Uparrow](\psi(n))$)}
  \end{align*}
  From $\rho \approx \rho' \in R_{\Gamma, S[\psi]}$, by the biconditional of $R_{\Gamma, S[\psi]}$:
  $\rho[\Uparrow] \approx \rho'[\Uparrow] \in R_\Gamma$.
  From $\semweak[\Gamma]{\psi}{\Delta}$:
  $\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho[\Uparrow])} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho'[\Uparrow])} \in R_\Delta$.
  This gives evidence $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}$.

  \emph{Head.}
  \begin{align*}
    &(\ensuremath{\llbracket q(\psi) \rrbracket(\rho)})(0) = \rho(0)
      && \text{(since $q(\psi)(0) = 0$)}
  \end{align*}
  From $\rho \approx \rho' \in R_{\Gamma, S[\psi]}$, by the biconditional of $R_{\Gamma, S[\psi]}$,
  there exists evidence $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}'$ such that
  $\rho(0) \approx \rho'(0) \in R_H^\Gamma(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}')$,
  where $R_H^\Gamma$ comes from
  $\ensuremath{\llbracket S[\psi] \rrbracket(\rho[\Uparrow])} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket S[\psi] \rrbracket(\rho'[\Uparrow])} \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_H^\Gamma(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}')$.

  By the head premise of $R_{\Delta, S}$ at $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}$ (using $\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho[\Uparrow])} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho'[\Uparrow])} \in R_\Delta$):
  $\ensuremath{\llbracket S \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho[\Uparrow])})} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket S \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho'[\Uparrow])})} \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_H^\Delta(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}})$.

  From the semantic well-formedness $\semtyeq[\Delta]{S}{S}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}$, instantiated as
  above (at $\Gamma$, $\semtyeq[\Gamma]{\psi}{\psi}{\Delta}$, $\rho[\Uparrow] \approx \rho'[\Uparrow]$),
  the type part gives in particular the commutation
  $\ensuremath{\llbracket S[\psi] \rrbracket(\rho[\Uparrow])} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket S \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho[\Uparrow])})} \in \mathcal{U}_i$.
  By \Cref{lem:univ-functional}, $R_H^\Gamma(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}') \Leftrightarrow R_H^\Delta(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}})$
  (both have the same left-hand domain type up to $\Leftrightarrow$).
  Hence $\rho(0) \approx \rho'(0) \in R_H^\Delta(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}})$.

title: Proof
body_md:

  $\Delta \approx \Delta \searrow R_\Delta$.
  By \Cref{lem:sem-ty-id} on $\semtyeq[\Delta]{S}{S}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}$: for every
  $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_\Delta :: \rho_0 \approx \rho_0' \in R_\Delta$, there is $R_H^\Delta(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_\Delta)$
  with $\ensuremath{\llbracket S \rrbracket(\rho_0)} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket S \rrbracket(\rho_0')} \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_H^\Delta(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_\Delta)$.
  By \textsc{Ctx-Ext}, this gives
  $(\Delta, x:S) \approx (\Delta, x:S) \searrow R_{\Delta,x:S}$.

  Let $\Gamma' \approx \Gamma' \searrow R'$, $\semweak[\Gamma']{\psi}{\Gamma}$,
  and $\rho \approx \rho' \in R'$ be given.

  \[
    \{\ensuremath{\llbracket (\sigma, t/x)[\psi] \rrbracket(\rho)},\;
    \ensuremath{\llbracket (\sigma, t/x) \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho)})},\;
    \ensuremath{\llbracket (\sigma', t'/x) \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho')})},\;
    \ensuremath{\llbracket (\sigma', t'/x)[\psi] \rrbracket(\rho')}\} \subseteq R_{\Delta, x:S}.
  \]
  Each of the four environments has the form (tail, head): the tail is the value of
  the underlying substitution on $\Delta$, and the head is the value at position $x$.
  By the biconditional of $R_{\Delta, x:S}$, it suffices to show
  the tails are pairwise related in $R_\Delta$ (yielding evidence $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}$) and the heads
  are related in $R_H^\Delta(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}})$.

  \emph{Tails.}
  Since $(\sigma, t/x)[\psi] = (\sigma[\psi], t[\psi]/x)$
  (by \Cref{lem:wk-subst-interact}), the four tail environments are:
  \[
    \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma[\psi] \rrbracket(\rho)}, \quad \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho)})}, \quad
    \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma' \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho')})}, \quad \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma'[\psi] \rrbracket(\rho')}.
  \]
  From $\semtyeq[\Gamma]{\sigma}{\sigma'}{\Delta}$ instantiated at $\Gamma'$, $\psi$, and
  $\rho \approx \rho' \in R'$:
  \[
    \{\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma[\psi] \rrbracket(\rho)},\; \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho)})},\;
    \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma' \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho')})},\; \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma'[\psi] \rrbracket(\rho')}\} \subseteq R_\Delta.
  \]
  In particular, the outer pair gives evidence
  $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}} :: \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma[\psi] \rrbracket(\rho)} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma'[\psi] \rrbracket(\rho')} \in R_\Delta$.

  \emph{Heads.}
  The four heads are:
  \[
    \ensuremath{\llbracket t[\psi] \rrbracket(\rho)}, \quad \ensuremath{\llbracket t \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho)})}, \quad
    \ensuremath{\llbracket t' \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho')})}, \quad \ensuremath{\llbracket t'[\psi] \rrbracket(\rho')}.
  \]
  We must show they are related in $R_H^\Delta(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}})$, where
  $R_H^\Delta(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}})$ comes from
  \[
    \ensuremath{\llbracket S \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma[\psi] \rrbracket(\rho)})} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket S \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma'[\psi] \rrbracket(\rho')})}
    \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_H^\Delta(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}).
  \]

  From $\semtyeq[\Gamma]{t}{t'}{S[\sigma]}$ at $\Gamma'$, $\psi$,
  $\rho \approx \rho' \in R'$, the type part gives some $R_t$ with
  $\ensuremath{\llbracket  \rrbracket(\rho)} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket S[\sigma] \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho)})} \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_t$
  (and analogous primed versions), and the term part gives
  \[
    \{\ensuremath{\llbracket t[\psi] \rrbracket(\rho)},\; \ensuremath{\llbracket t \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho)})},\;
    \ensuremath{\llbracket t' \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho')})},\; \ensuremath{\llbracket t'[\psi] \rrbracket(\rho')}\} \subseteq R_t.
  \]

  It remains to show $R_t \Leftrightarrow R_H^\Delta(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}})$.
  Note that $\ensuremath{\llbracket  \rrbracket(\rho)} = \ensuremath{\llbracket S[\sigma[\psi]] \rrbracket(\rho)}$
  (by \Cref{lem:wk-subst-comm}).
  By \Cref{lem:sem-wk-subst}, we have
  $\semtyeq[\Gamma']{\sigma[\psi]}{\sigma'[\psi]}{\Delta}$.
  Instantiating $\semtyeq[\Delta]{S}{S}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}$ at $\Gamma'$, this semantic substitution,
  and $\rho \approx \rho' \in R'$: the type part gives the commutation
  \[
    \ensuremath{\llbracket S[\sigma[\psi]] \rrbracket(\rho)} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket S \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma[\psi] \rrbracket(\rho)})} \in \mathcal{U}_i.
  \]
  Hence $R_t$ (from $\ensuremath{\llbracket S[\sigma[\psi]] \rrbracket(\rho)}$) and $R_H^\Delta(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}})$ (from
  $\ensuremath{\llbracket S \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma[\psi] \rrbracket(\rho)})}$) have related left-hand types in $\mathcal{U}_i$;
  by \Cref{lem:univ-functional}, $R_t \Leftrightarrow R_H^\Delta(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}})$.
  Therefore the four heads are in $R_H^\Delta(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}})$.

title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:sem-ext-pre}
  If $\semtyeq[\Gamma]{\sigma}{\sigma'}{\Delta}$ and
  $\semtyeq[\Delta]{t}{t'}{T}$, then
  $\semtyeq[\Gamma]{(\sigma, t[\sigma]/x)}{(\sigma', t'[\sigma']/x)}{\Delta, x : T}$.
head: environment
name: Extension by precomposed term

title: Proof
body_md:
By \Cref{lem:sem-ty-id} on $\semtyeq[\Delta]{t}{t'}{T}$,
  for any $\rho_0 \approx \rho_0' \in R_\Delta$:
  $\ensuremath{\llbracket T \rrbracket(\rho_0)} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket T \rrbracket(\rho_0')} \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_H^\Delta$.
  By \textsc{Ctx-Ext}, this yields
  $(\Delta, x:T) \approx (\Delta, x:T) \searrow R_{\Delta,x:T}$.

  Let $\Gamma' \approx \Gamma' \searrow R'$, $\semweak[\Gamma']{\psi}{\Gamma}$,
  and $\rho \approx \rho' \in R'$ be given.
  We must show:
  \[
    \{\ensuremath{\llbracket (\sigma, t[\sigma]/x)[\psi] \rrbracket(\rho)},\;
    \ensuremath{\llbracket (\sigma, t[\sigma]/x) \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho)})},\;
    \ensuremath{\llbracket (\sigma', t'[\sigma']/x) \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho')})},\;
    \ensuremath{\llbracket (\sigma', t'[\sigma']/x)[\psi] \rrbracket(\rho')}\} \subseteq R_{\Delta, x:T}.
  \]
  By the biconditional of $R_{\Delta, x:T}$ (with respect to the substitution
  extensions $(\sigma, t[\sigma]/x)$, etc.), it suffices to exhibit evidence
  $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}} :: \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma[\psi] \rrbracket(\rho)} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma'[\psi] \rrbracket(\rho')} \in R_\Delta$
  --- relating the tails of the outer pair of substitution evaluations --- and to show
  that the four head values
  $\ensuremath{\llbracket t[\sigma][\psi] \rrbracket(\rho)}, \ensuremath{\llbracket t[\sigma] \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho)})},
  \ensuremath{\llbracket t'[\sigma'] \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho')})}, \ensuremath{\llbracket t'[\sigma'][\psi] \rrbracket(\rho')}$
  are pairwise related in the head PER $R_H^\Delta(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}})$, which is the PER returned by
  $\ensuremath{\llbracket T \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma[\psi] \rrbracket(\rho)})} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket T \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma'[\psi] \rrbracket(\rho')})}
   \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_H^\Delta(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}})$.

  \emph{Tails.}
  \begin{align*}
    &(\sigma, t[\sigma]/x)[\psi] = (\sigma[\psi], t[\sigma][\psi]/x)
      && \text{(by \Cref{lem:wk-subst-interact})}
  \end{align*}
  So the four tails are $\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma[\psi] \rrbracket(\rho)}, \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho)})},
  \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma' \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho')})}, \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma'[\psi] \rrbracket(\rho')}$.
  By $\semtyeq[\Gamma]{\sigma}{\sigma'}{\Delta}$ at $\Gamma'$, $\psi$, $\rho \approx \rho'$:
  \[
    \{\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma[\psi] \rrbracket(\rho)},\, \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho)})},\,
    \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma' \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho')})},\, \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma'[\psi] \rrbracket(\rho')}\} \subseteq R_\Delta,
  \]
  with witness
  $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}} :: \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma[\psi] \rrbracket(\rho)} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma'[\psi] \rrbracket(\rho')} \in R_\Delta$.

  \emph{Heads.}
  We instantiate $\semtyeq[\Delta]{t}{t'}{T}$ in two ways and bridge the resulting
  four-value patterns through a shared inner value.

  \emph{First instantiation} of $\semtyeq[\Delta]{t}{t'}{T}$:
  at $\Gamma'$, the semantic substitution
  $\semtyeq[\Gamma']{\sigma[\psi]}{\sigma'[\psi]}{\Delta}$ (\Cref{lem:sem-wk-subst}),
  and $\rho \approx \rho' \in R'$.
  The type part gives some $R_t$ with
  \[
    \ensuremath{\llbracket T[\sigma[\psi]] \rrbracket(\rho)} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket T \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma[\psi] \rrbracket(\rho)})}
    \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_t,
  \]
  and the term part gives
  \[
    \{\ensuremath{\llbracket t[\sigma[\psi]] \rrbracket(\rho)},\, \ensuremath{\llbracket t \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma[\psi] \rrbracket(\rho)})},\,
    \ensuremath{\llbracket t' \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma'[\psi] \rrbracket(\rho')})},\, \ensuremath{\llbracket t'[\sigma'[\psi]] \rrbracket(\rho')}\} \subseteq R_t.
  \]
  By \Cref{lem:univ-functional} (same left type $\ensuremath{\llbracket T \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma[\psi] \rrbracket(\rho)})}$),
  $R_t \Leftrightarrow R_H^\Delta(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}})$.
  By \Cref{lem:wk-subst-comm}, $t[\sigma][\psi] = t[\sigma[\psi]]$, so the outer values
  match: $\ensuremath{\llbracket t[\sigma][\psi] \rrbracket(\rho)} = \ensuremath{\llbracket t[\sigma[\psi]] \rrbracket(\rho)}$
  (and similarly for the primed side).
  Hence the outer pair of goal heads and the inner pair
  $\ensuremath{\llbracket t \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma[\psi] \rrbracket(\rho)})}, \ensuremath{\llbracket t' \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma'[\psi] \rrbracket(\rho')})}$
  are all in $R_H^\Delta(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}})$.

  \emph{Second instantiation} of $\semtyeq[\Delta]{t}{t'}{T}$:
  at $\Gamma$ (with $R_\Gamma$, from $\semweak[\Gamma']{\psi}{\Gamma}$), the semantic
  substitution $\sigma \approx \sigma' : \Delta$ (the hypothesis), and
  $\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho)} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho')} \in R_\Gamma$.
  The type part gives some $R_t'$ with
  \[
    \ensuremath{\llbracket T[\sigma] \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho)})} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket T \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho)})})}
    \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_t',
  \]
  and the term part gives
  \[
    \{\ensuremath{\llbracket t[\sigma] \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho)})},\, \ensuremath{\llbracket t \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho)})})},\,
    \ensuremath{\llbracket t' \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma' \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho')})})},\, \ensuremath{\llbracket t'[\sigma'] \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho')})}\}
    \subseteq R_t'.
  \]
  Since $\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma[\psi] \rrbracket(\rho)}$ and $\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho)})}$ are both in
  $R_\Delta$ (related by the tails part), by \Cref{lem:univ-functional} applied to the
  two type evaluations (the head premise of $R_{\Delta, x:T}$ at the appropriate
  evidence), $R_t' \Leftrightarrow R_H^\Delta(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}})$.
  This places the inner pair $\ensuremath{\llbracket t[\sigma] \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho)})}, \ensuremath{\llbracket t'[\sigma'] \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho')})}$
  of goal heads in $R_H^\Delta(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}})$.

  \emph{Bridging the two instantiations.}
  The shared inner value $\ensuremath{\llbracket t \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho)})})}$ appears in both
  $R_t$ (as the inner-left of the first instantiation, after using
  $\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma[\psi] \rrbracket(\rho)} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho)})} \in R_\Delta$ and
  right irrelevance) and $R_t'$ (as the inner-left of the second instantiation).
  Both $R_t$ and $R_t'$ are equivalent to $R_H^\Delta(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}})$, so by transitivity of
  $R_H^\Delta(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}})$ through this shared value, all four goal heads are related.

title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:sem-q}
  If $\semtyeq[\Gamma]{\sigma}{\sigma'}{\Delta}$ and
  $\semtyeq[\Delta]{S}{S}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}$, then
  $\semtyeq[\Gamma, x:S[\sigma]]{q(\sigma)}{q(\sigma')}{\Delta, x:S}$.
head: environment
name: Lifting is semantic

title: Proof
body_md:
We first establish the context PER for $\Gamma, x:S[\sigma]$.
  From $\semtyeq[\Gamma]{\sigma}{\sigma'}{\Delta}$ we have
  $\Gamma \approx \Gamma \searrow R_\Gamma$.
  Apply $\semtyeq[\Delta]{S}{S}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}$ at $\Gamma$ (with $R_\Gamma$), the semantic
  substitution $\semtyeq[\Gamma]{\sigma}{\sigma}{\Delta}$ (the reflexive instance,
  obtained from $\semtyeq[\Gamma]{\sigma}{\sigma'}{\Delta}$ via symmetry and
  transitivity, \Cref{lem:sem-sym,lem:sem-trans}), and any
  $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_\Gamma :: \rho_0 \approx \rho_0' \in R_\Gamma$:
  the type part gives, in particular,
  $\ensuremath{\llbracket S[\sigma] \rrbracket(\rho_0)} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket S[\sigma] \rrbracket(\rho_0')}
  \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_H^\Gamma(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_\Gamma)$
  for some head family $R_H^\Gamma$.
  By \textsc{Ctx-Ext}, this yields
  $(\Gamma, x:S[\sigma]) \approx (\Gamma, x:S[\sigma]) \searrow R_{\Gamma, x:S[\sigma]}$
  with the biconditional
  \begin{align*}
    &\rho_1 \approx \rho_1' \in R_{\Gamma, x:S[\sigma]}
      \;\leftrightarrow\;
      (\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_\Gamma :: \rho_1[\Uparrow] \approx \rho_1'[\Uparrow] \in R_\Gamma
        \;\wedge\;
        \rho_1(0) \approx \rho_1'(0) \in R_H^\Gamma(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_\Gamma)).
  \end{align*}

  By an analogous construction (or directly by \Cref{lem:sem-ty-id} on
  $\semtyeq[\Delta]{S}{S}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}$ followed by \textsc{Ctx-Ext}), we also obtain
  $(\Delta, x:S) \approx (\Delta, x:S) \searrow R_{\Delta, x:S}$ with head family
  $R_H^\Delta$, where for every $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_\Delta :: \rho_0 \approx \rho_0' \in R_\Delta$,
  $R_H^\Delta(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_\Delta)$ is determined by
  $\ensuremath{\llbracket S \rrbracket(\rho_0)} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket S \rrbracket(\rho_0')} \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_H^\Delta(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_\Delta)$,
  with biconditional
  \begin{align*}
    &\rho_1 \approx \rho_1' \in R_{\Delta, x:S}
      \;\leftrightarrow\;
      (\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_\Delta :: \rho_1[\Uparrow] \approx \rho_1'[\Uparrow] \in R_\Delta
        \;\wedge\;
        \rho_1(0) \approx \rho_1'(0) \in R_H^\Delta(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_\Delta)).
  \end{align*}
  Here $R_\Delta$ comes from the premise $\semtyeq[\Gamma]{\sigma}{\sigma'}{\Delta}$
  (which carries $\Delta \approx \Delta \searrow R_\Delta$).

  We now show $\semtyeq[\Gamma, x:S[\sigma]]{q(\sigma)}{q(\sigma')}{\Delta, x:S}$ by
  unfolding the conclusion.
  Recall $q(\sigma) = (\sigma[\Uparrow], x_0/x)$.
  By \Cref{lem:wk-subst-interact}\,(2), $(\sigma[\Uparrow], x_0/x)[\psi]
  = (\sigma[\Uparrow][\psi], x_0[\psi]/x) = (\sigma[\Uparrow \circ \psi], \psi(0)/x)$
  for any weakening $\psi$ (using $\sigma[\Uparrow][\psi] = \sigma[\Uparrow \circ \psi]$
  by associativity of post-composition with weakenings, and $x_0[\psi] = \psi(0)$).

  We must show: for every context $\Gamma'$ with
  $\Gamma' \approx \Gamma' \searrow R'$, every
  $\semweak[\Gamma']{\psi}{\Gamma, x:S[\sigma]}$, and every
  $\rho \approx \rho' \in R'$,
  the four values
  \[
    \ensuremath{\llbracket q(\sigma)[\psi] \rrbracket(\rho)},\;
    \ensuremath{\llbracket q(\sigma) \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho)})},\;
    \ensuremath{\llbracket q(\sigma') \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho')})},\;
    \ensuremath{\llbracket q(\sigma')[\psi] \rrbracket(\rho')}
  \]
  lie in $R_{\Delta, x:S}$.

  By definition of $\semweak[\Gamma']{\psi}{\Gamma, x:S[\sigma]}$,
  $\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho)} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho')} \in R_{\Gamma, x:S[\sigma]}$.
  By the biconditional of $R_{\Gamma, x:S[\sigma]}$ established above, this gives
  \begin{align*}
    &\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_\Gamma :: (\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho)})[\Uparrow] \approx (\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho')})[\Uparrow] \in R_\Gamma
      && \text{(tail)} \\
    &(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho)})(0) \approx (\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho')})(0) \in R_H^\Gamma(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_\Gamma)
      && \text{(head)}
  \end{align*}

  By \Cref{lem:sem-wk-shift}, $\semweak[\Gamma, x:S[\sigma]]{\Uparrow}{\Gamma}$.
  By \Cref{lem:sem-wk-comp}, $\semweak[\Gamma']{\Uparrow \circ \psi}{\Gamma}$, where
  $\Uparrow \circ \psi$ is the composition of weakenings.

  We must show the goal four values lie in $R_{\Delta, x:S}$.
  By the biconditional of $R_{\Delta, x:S}$ recalled above, this requires evidence
  $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_\Delta$ relating the four \emph{tails} in $R_\Delta$ and the four \emph{heads}
  in $R_H^\Delta(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_\Delta)$.

  \emph{Tails.}
  We compute the four tails using the pointwise identities above.
  For an extended substitution $(\tau, t/x)$, the evaluation
  $\ensuremath{\llbracket (\tau, t/x) \rrbracket(\rho_0)}$ is the environment with head $\ensuremath{\llbracket t \rrbracket(\rho_0)}$ at
  index $0$ and tail $\ensuremath{\llbracket \tau \rrbracket(\rho_0)}$ at indices $1, 2, \ldots$;
  hence $(\ensuremath{\llbracket (\tau, t/x) \rrbracket(\rho_0)})[\Uparrow] = \ensuremath{\llbracket \tau \rrbracket(\rho_0)}$.
  Applied to the four goal values:
  \begin{align*}
    &(\ensuremath{\llbracket q(\sigma)[\psi] \rrbracket(\rho)})[\Uparrow]
      = \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma[\Uparrow \circ \psi] \rrbracket(\rho)}, \\
    &(\ensuremath{\llbracket q(\sigma) \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho)})})[\Uparrow]
      = \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma[\Uparrow] \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho)})}, \\
    &(\ensuremath{\llbracket q(\sigma') \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho')})})[\Uparrow]
      = \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma'[\Uparrow] \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho')})}, \\
    &(\ensuremath{\llbracket q(\sigma')[\psi] \rrbracket(\rho')})[\Uparrow]
      = \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma'[\Uparrow \circ \psi] \rrbracket(\rho')}.
  \end{align*}

  \emph{First instantiation} of $\semtyeq[\Gamma]{\sigma}{\sigma'}{\Delta}$:
  at $\Gamma'$, the semantic weakening $\semweak[\Gamma']{\Uparrow \circ \psi}{\Gamma}$,
  and $\rho \approx \rho' \in R'$:
  \[
    \{\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma[\Uparrow \circ \psi] \rrbracket(\rho)},\;
    \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \Uparrow \circ \psi \rrbracket(\rho)})},\;
    \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma' \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \Uparrow \circ \psi \rrbracket(\rho')})},\;
    \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma'[\Uparrow \circ \psi] \rrbracket(\rho')}\} \subseteq R_\Delta.
  \]
  Since $\Uparrow \circ \psi$ is a weakening, by the definition of weakening
  evaluation, $\ensuremath{\llbracket \Uparrow \circ \psi \rrbracket(\rho_0)} = (\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho_0)})[\Uparrow]$
  for any $\rho_0$ (verified pointwise:
  $\ensuremath{\llbracket \Uparrow \circ \psi \rrbracket(\rho_0)}(n) = \rho_0((\Uparrow \circ \psi)(n))
  = \rho_0(\psi(n+1)) = (\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho_0)})[\Uparrow](n)$).
  So this first instantiation gives the outer two tails of the goal, plus
  intermediate values $\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket((\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho)})[\Uparrow])}$ and
  $\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma' \rrbracket((\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho')})[\Uparrow])}$.

  \emph{Second instantiation} of $\semtyeq[\Gamma]{\sigma}{\sigma'}{\Delta}$:
  at $\Gamma, x:S[\sigma]$ (using $R_{\Gamma, x:S[\sigma]}$), the semantic weakening
  $\semweak[\Gamma, x:S[\sigma]]{\Uparrow}{\Gamma}$, and the related environments
  $\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho)} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho')} \in R_{\Gamma, x:S[\sigma]}$:
  \[
    \{\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma[\Uparrow] \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho)})},\;
    \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \Uparrow \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho)})})},\;
    \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma' \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \Uparrow \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho')})})},\;
    \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma'[\Uparrow] \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho')})}\} \subseteq R_\Delta.
  \]
  Since $\Uparrow$ is a weakening, $\ensuremath{\llbracket \Uparrow \rrbracket(\rho_0)} = \rho_0[\Uparrow]$
  for any $\rho_0$.  So this second instantiation gives the inner two tails of the
  goal, plus the intermediate values $\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket((\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho)})[\Uparrow])}$
  and $\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma' \rrbracket((\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho')})[\Uparrow])}$.

  The intermediate inner-left value
  $\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket((\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho)})[\Uparrow])}$ appears in both instantiations
  (since $\ensuremath{\llbracket \Uparrow \circ \psi \rrbracket(\rho)} = (\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho)})[\Uparrow]
  = \ensuremath{\llbracket \Uparrow \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho)})}$).
  By symmetry (\Cref{lem:ctx-sym}) and transitivity (\Cref{lem:ctx-trans}) of $R_\Delta$
  through this shared value, all four tails are pairwise related in $R_\Delta$.
  In particular, the outer pair gives evidence
  $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_\Delta :: \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma[\Uparrow \circ \psi] \rrbracket(\rho)}
  \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma'[\Uparrow \circ \psi] \rrbracket(\rho')} \in R_\Delta$.

  \emph{Heads.}
  The four heads of the goal four values are:
  \begin{align*}
    &\ensuremath{\llbracket q(\sigma)[\psi] \rrbracket(\rho)}(0) = \ensuremath{\llbracket \psi(0) \rrbracket(\rho)} = \rho(\psi(0)) = (\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho)})(0), \\
    &\ensuremath{\llbracket q(\sigma) \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho)})}(0) = \ensuremath{\llbracket x_0 \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho)})} = (\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho)})(0),
  \end{align*}
  and analogously for the primed pair.
  All four heads collapse to $(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho)})(0)$ and $(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho')})(0)$.
  By the head clause of the biconditional of $R_{\Gamma, x:S[\sigma]}$ recalled
  above, $(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho)})(0) \approx (\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho')})(0) \in R_H^\Gamma(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_\Gamma)$.

  \emph{Bridging head PERs.}
  It remains to show $R_H^\Gamma(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_\Gamma) \Leftrightarrow R_H^\Delta(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_\Delta)$,
  so that the four heads all lie in $R_H^\Delta(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_\Delta)$.
  Apply $\semtyeq[\Delta]{S}{S}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}$ at $\Gamma$ (using $R_\Gamma$, available
  from $\semweak[\Gamma, x:S[\sigma]]{\Uparrow}{\Gamma}$), the semantic substitution
  $\semtyeq[\Gamma]{\sigma}{\sigma}{\Delta}$ (a special case of the hypothesis ---
  formally, applying the hypothesis along with reflexivity by symmetry/transitivity
  to obtain the reflexive instance), and the related environments
  $(\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho)})[\Uparrow] \approx (\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho')})[\Uparrow] \in R_\Gamma$
  (from $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_\Gamma$): the type part gives the commutation
  \[
    \ensuremath{\llbracket S[\sigma] \rrbracket((\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho)})[\Uparrow])} \approx
    \ensuremath{\llbracket S \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket((\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho)})[\Uparrow])})}
    \in \mathcal{U}_i.
  \]
  The right-hand side is $\ensuremath{\llbracket S \rrbracket(\rho_0)}$ where
  $\rho_0 = \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket((\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho)})[\Uparrow])}$, which is in $R_\Delta$ via
  the second instantiation; by definition of $R_H^\Delta(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_\Delta)$, this lands in
  $\mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_H^\Delta(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_\Delta)$.
  The left-hand side $\ensuremath{\llbracket S[\sigma] \rrbracket((\ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho)})[\Uparrow])}$ lands in
  $\mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_H^\Gamma(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_\Gamma)$ by definition of $R_H^\Gamma$.
  By \Cref{lem:univ-functional}, $R_H^\Gamma(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_\Gamma) \Leftrightarrow R_H^\Delta(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_\Delta)$.
  Hence all four heads are in $R_H^\Delta(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_\Delta)$.

  Combining tails and heads via the biconditional of $R_{\Delta, x:S}$, the four
  goal values are in $R_{\Delta, x:S}$.

body_md:
Let $\Gamma' \approx \Gamma' \searrow R'$,
  $\semtyeq[\Gamma']{\sigma}{\sigma'}{\Gamma}$, and $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}} :: \rho \approx \rho' \in R'$.
  From the hypothesis:
  \[
    \{\ensuremath{\llbracket t[\sigma] \rrbracket(\rho)},\; \ensuremath{\llbracket t \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\rho)})},\;
    \ensuremath{\llbracket t' \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma' \rrbracket(\rho')})},\; \ensuremath{\llbracket t'[\sigma'] \rrbracket(\rho')}\} \subseteq R_T.
  \]
  We need:
  \[
    \{\ensuremath{\llbracket t'[\sigma] \rrbracket(\rho)},\; \ensuremath{\llbracket t' \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\rho)})},\;
    \ensuremath{\llbracket t \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma' \rrbracket(\rho')})},\; \ensuremath{\llbracket t[\sigma'] \rrbracket(\rho')}\} \subseteq R_T.
  \]

  Apply the hypothesis at $\sigma' \approx \sigma$ (using \Cref{lem:sem-sym}) and
  $\rho' \approx \rho$ (using symmetry of $R'$):
  \[
    \{\ensuremath{\llbracket t[\sigma'] \rrbracket(\rho')},\; \ensuremath{\llbracket t \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma' \rrbracket(\rho')})},\;
    \ensuremath{\llbracket t' \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\rho)})},\; \ensuremath{\llbracket t'[\sigma] \rrbracket(\rho)}\} \subseteq R_T.
  \]
  By symmetry of $R_T$ (\Cref{lem:univ-sym}), we can reverse the order:
  \[
    \{\ensuremath{\llbracket t'[\sigma] \rrbracket(\rho)},\; \ensuremath{\llbracket t' \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\rho)})},\;
    \ensuremath{\llbracket t \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma' \rrbracket(\rho')})},\; \ensuremath{\llbracket t[\sigma'] \rrbracket(\rho')}\} \subseteq R_T.
    \qedhere
  \]

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\Gamma' \approx \Gamma' \searrow R'$,
  $\semtyeq[\Gamma']{\sigma}{\sigma'}{\Gamma}$, and
  $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}} :: \rho \approx \rho' \in R'$ be given.
  We must show that the four type values
  \[
    \{\ensuremath{\llbracket \ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}[\sigma] \rrbracket(\rho)},\;
    \ensuremath{\llbracket \ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}} \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\rho)})},\;
    \ensuremath{\llbracket \ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}} \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma' \rrbracket(\rho')})},\;
    \ensuremath{\llbracket \ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}[\sigma'] \rrbracket(\rho')}\}
    \subseteq \mathcal{U}_{1+i} \searrow R_T
  \]
  for some $R_T$ with $R_T \Leftrightarrow \mathcal{U}_i$ (as in \Cref{lem:fund-u-wf}),
  and that the four term values
  \[
    \{\ensuremath{\llbracket (\Pi(x:S).\,T)[\sigma] \rrbracket(\rho)},\;
    \ensuremath{\llbracket \Pi(x:S).\,T \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\rho)})},\;
    \ensuremath{\llbracket \Pi(x:S').\,T' \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma' \rrbracket(\rho')})},\;
    \ensuremath{\llbracket (\Pi(x:S').\,T')[\sigma'] \rrbracket(\rho')}\}
    \subseteq R_T,
  \]
  i.e.\ relate in $\mathcal{U}_i \searrow R$ for some $R$.

  \emph{Type part.}
  As in \Cref{lem:fund-u-wf}, the four values of $\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}$ collapse to $U_i$,
  and $U_i \approx U_i \in \mathcal{U}_{1+i} \searrow R_T$ with $R_T \Leftrightarrow \mathcal{U}_i$
  by \textsc{U-Univ}.

  \emph{Term part.}
  We compute the four term values:
  \begin{align*}
    &\ensuremath{\llbracket (\Pi(x:S).\,T)[\sigma] \rrbracket(\rho)}
      = \ensuremath{\llbracket \Pi(x:S[\sigma]).\,(T[q(\sigma)]) \rrbracket(\rho)}
      && \text{(by definition of substitution on $\Pi$)} \\
    &\quad= \Pi(\ensuremath{\llbracket S[\sigma] \rrbracket(\rho)},\; T[q(\sigma)],\; \rho)
      && \text{(by evaluation of $\Pi$)} \\[4pt]
    &\ensuremath{\llbracket \Pi(x:S).\,T \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\rho)})} \\
    & \quad = \Pi(\ensuremath{\llbracket S \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\rho)})},\; T,\; \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\rho)})
      && \text{(by evaluation of $\Pi$)}
  \end{align*}
  Analogous computations apply to the primed pair, yielding
  \[
    \Pi(\ensuremath{\llbracket S' \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma' \rrbracket(\rho')})}, T', \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma' \rrbracket(\rho')})
    \quad \text{and} \quad
    \Pi(\ensuremath{\llbracket S'[\sigma'] \rrbracket(\rho')}, T'[q(\sigma')], \rho').
  \]

  We construct a \textsc{U-Pi} derivation relating the outermost two values; the
  inner two follow analogously.

  \emph{Domain.}
  Apply $\semtyeq[\Gamma]{S}{S'}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}$ at $\Gamma'$, $\sigma \approx \sigma' :
  \Gamma$, and $\rho \approx \rho' \in R'$:
  \begin{align*}
    &\{\ensuremath{\llbracket S[\sigma] \rrbracket(\rho)},\; \ensuremath{\llbracket S \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\rho)})},\;
      \ensuremath{\llbracket S' \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma' \rrbracket(\rho')})},\; \ensuremath{\llbracket S'[\sigma'] \rrbracket(\rho')}\}
      \subseteq \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_I
      && \text{(by hypothesis on $S, S'$)}
  \end{align*}

  \emph{Codomain via lifting.}
  By \Cref{lem:sem-q} on $\semtyeq[\Gamma']{\sigma}{\sigma'}{\Gamma}$ and
  $\semtyeq[\Gamma]{S}{S'}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}$ (using its reflexive instance
  $\semtyeq[\Gamma]{S}{S}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}$ via \Cref{lem:sem-sym,lem:sem-trans} for the
  well-formedness premise of \Cref{lem:sem-q}):
  \[
    \semtyeq[\Gamma', x:S[\sigma]]{q(\sigma)}{q(\sigma')}{\Gamma, x:S}.
  \]
  By the first premise of the semantic substitution judgment, this carries
  $(\Gamma', x:S[\sigma]) \approx (\Gamma', x:S[\sigma]) \searrow R_{\Gamma',x:S[\sigma]}$
  and $(\Gamma, x:S) \approx (\Gamma, x:S) \searrow R_{\Gamma,x:S}$.

  Let $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_I :: a \approx a' \in R_I$ be given.
  By the biconditional of $R_{\Gamma',x:S[\sigma]}$ from \textsc{Ctx-Ext},
  $(\rho, a/x) \approx (\rho', a'/x) \in R_{\Gamma',x:S[\sigma]}$ requires
  $\rho \approx \rho' \in R'$ (which we have) and
  $a \approx a' \in R_H'(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}')$ where $R_H'$ is the head family for
  $R_{\Gamma',x:S[\sigma]}$, governed by
  $\ensuremath{\llbracket S[\sigma] \rrbracket(\rho)} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket S[\sigma] \rrbracket(\rho')} \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_H'(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}')$
  (with $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}' :: \rho \approx \rho' \in R'$).
  By \Cref{lem:univ-functional} on the same left type $\ensuremath{\llbracket S[\sigma] \rrbracket(\rho)}$ that
  governs both $R_I$ (from the domain step) and $R_H'(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}')$,
  $R_I \Leftrightarrow R_H'(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}')$.
  Hence $a \approx a' \in R_H'(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}')$, and
  $(\rho, a/x) \approx (\rho', a'/x) \in R_{\Gamma',x:S[\sigma]}$.

  Apply $\semtyeq[\Gamma, x:S]{T}{T'}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}$ at $\Gamma', x:S[\sigma]$ (with
  $R_{\Gamma',x:S[\sigma]}$), the lifted substitution
  $\semtyeq[\Gamma', x:S[\sigma]]{q(\sigma)}{q(\sigma')}{\Gamma, x:S}$, and
  $(\rho, a/x) \approx (\rho', a'/x) \in R_{\Gamma',x:S[\sigma]}$:
  \begin{align*}
    &\{\ensuremath{\llbracket T[q(\sigma)] \rrbracket((\rho, a/x))},\;
      \ensuremath{\llbracket T \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket q(\sigma) \rrbracket((\rho, a/x))})},\\
    &\quad \ensuremath{\llbracket T' \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket q(\sigma') \rrbracket((\rho', a'/x))})},\;
      \ensuremath{\llbracket T'[q(\sigma')] \rrbracket((\rho', a'/x))}\}
      \subseteq \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_I)
      && \text{(by hypothesis on $T, T'$)}
  \end{align*}
  The outer two values $\ensuremath{\llbracket T[q(\sigma)] \rrbracket((\rho, a/x))}$ and
  $\ensuremath{\llbracket T'[q(\sigma')] \rrbracket((\rho', a'/x))}$ are exactly the codomain expressions of the
  outer $\Pi$-values applied to $a, a'$, satisfying the \textsc{U-Pi} codomain premise
  for the outer pair.

  For the inner $\Pi$-values $\Pi(\ensuremath{\llbracket S \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\rho)})}, T, \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\rho)})$
  (left) and $\Pi(\ensuremath{\llbracket S' \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma' \rrbracket(\rho')})}, T', \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma' \rrbracket(\rho')})$
  (right), the codomain expressions applied to $a, a'$ are
  $\ensuremath{\llbracket T \rrbracket((\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\rho)}, a/x))}$ and $\ensuremath{\llbracket T' \rrbracket((\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma' \rrbracket(\rho')}, a'/x))}$.
  Applying the lifted-substitution four-value pattern (instantiated at the identity
  weakening on $\Gamma', x:S[\sigma]$ with $(\rho, a/x) \approx (\rho', a'/x)$), we
  obtain in particular
  \[
    \ensuremath{\llbracket q(\sigma) \rrbracket((\rho, a/x))} \approx (\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\rho)}, a/x)
    \in R_{\Gamma, x:S}
  \]
  (the outer-versus-inner relatedness in that four-value pattern).
  By \Cref{lem:sem-ty-id} on $\semtyeq[\Gamma, x:S]{T}{T}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}$ applied to this
  related pair:
  \[
    \ensuremath{\llbracket T \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket q(\sigma) \rrbracket((\rho, a/x))})} \approx
    \ensuremath{\llbracket T \rrbracket((\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\rho)}, a/x))} \in \mathcal{U}_i.
  \]
  Combined with the inner-pair relatedness from the codomain
  four-value pattern
  \[
    \ensuremath{\llbracket T \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket q(\sigma) \rrbracket((\rho, a/x))})} \approx
    \ensuremath{\llbracket T' \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket q(\sigma') \rrbracket((\rho', a'/x))})}
    \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_I)
  \]
  and the analogous identity
  \[
    \ensuremath{\llbracket T' \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket q(\sigma') \rrbracket((\rho', a'/x))})} \approx
    \ensuremath{\llbracket T' \rrbracket((\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma' \rrbracket(\rho')}, a'/x))} \in \mathcal{U}_i
  \]
  on the primed
  side (by \Cref{lem:sem-ty-id} on the reflexive
  $\semtyeq[\Gamma, x:S]{T'}{T'}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}$ obtained from
  $\semtyeq[\Gamma, x:S]{T}{T'}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}$ by symmetry/transitivity),
  symmetry and transitivity of $\mathcal{U}_i$ yield
  \[
    \ensuremath{\llbracket T \rrbracket((\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\rho)}, a/x))} \approx
    \ensuremath{\llbracket T' \rrbracket((\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma' \rrbracket(\rho')}, a'/x))} \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_I).
  \]
  This is the \textsc{U-Pi} codomain premise for the inner pair.

  \emph{Function PER.}
  Define $R$ by the biconditional:
  $f \approx f' \in R \;\leftrightarrow\;
  (\forall \ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_I :: a \approx a' \in R_I.\; f \cdot a \approx f' \cdot a' \in R_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_I))$.

  \emph{Outer pair.}
  By \textsc{U-Pi} applied with domain $R_I$ (from \emph{Domain}) and codomain
  $R_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_I)$ (from the outer pair of the codomain four-value pattern):
  \[
    \Pi(\ensuremath{\llbracket S[\sigma] \rrbracket(\rho)},\, T[q(\sigma)],\, \rho)
    \approx \Pi(\ensuremath{\llbracket S'[\sigma'] \rrbracket(\rho')},\, T'[q(\sigma')],\, \rho')
    \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R.
  \]

  \emph{Inner pair.}
  By \textsc{U-Pi} applied with domain $R_I$ (the inner pair
  $\ensuremath{\llbracket S \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\rho)})} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket S' \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma' \rrbracket(\rho')})} \in \mathcal{U}_i$
  from \emph{Domain} also lands in $R_I$ by \Cref{lem:univ-functional}) and codomain
  $R_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_I)$ (just derived for the inner pair):
  \[
    \Pi(\ensuremath{\llbracket S \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\rho)})},\, T,\, \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\rho)})
    \approx \Pi(\ensuremath{\llbracket S' \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma' \rrbracket(\rho')})},\, T',\, \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma' \rrbracket(\rho')})
    \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R.
  \]

  \emph{Cross-relations.}
  We have established $\Pi$-relatedness for the outer pair and for the inner pair,
  both with element PER $R$.
  To get full four-way relatedness, we establish one cross-relation
  (outer-left versus inner-left) via a third \textsc{U-Pi} derivation; the
  remaining cross-relations follow by symmetry (\Cref{lem:univ-sym}) and
  transitivity (\Cref{lem:univ-trans}) of $\mathcal{U}_i$.

  The third \textsc{U-Pi} derivation uses:
  \begin{itemize}
  \@idxitem \emph{Domain.}
    From the \emph{Domain} four-value pattern (in
    $\mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_I$), the cross relation
    \[
      \ensuremath{\llbracket S[\sigma] \rrbracket(\rho)} \approx
      \ensuremath{\llbracket S \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\rho)})} \in \mathcal{U}_i
    \]
    holds, with element PER $R_I$ by \Cref{lem:univ-functional}.
  \@idxitem \emph{Codomain.}
    Let $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_I :: a \approx a' \in R_I$.
    We must show
    \[
      \ensuremath{\llbracket T[q(\sigma)] \rrbracket((\rho, a/x))} \approx
      \ensuremath{\llbracket T \rrbracket((\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\rho)}, a'/x))}
      \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_I).
    \]
    From the codomain four-value pattern, the cross relation
    \[
      \ensuremath{\llbracket T[q(\sigma)] \rrbracket((\rho, a/x))} \approx
      \ensuremath{\llbracket T \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket q(\sigma') \rrbracket((\rho', a'/x))})}
      \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_I)
    \]
    holds (outer-left versus inner-right).
    By \Cref{lem:sem-ty-id} applied at the relatedness
    $\ensuremath{\llbracket q(\sigma') \rrbracket((\rho', a'/x))} \approx (\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\rho)}, a'/x)
    \in R_{\Gamma, x:S}$ (which holds by symmetry and transitivity in
    $R_{\Gamma, x:S}$, bridging through the inner-pair relatedness of the lifted
    substitution four-value pattern):
    \[
      \ensuremath{\llbracket T \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket q(\sigma') \rrbracket((\rho', a'/x))})} \approx
      \ensuremath{\llbracket T \rrbracket((\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\rho)}, a'/x))} \in \mathcal{U}_i.
    \]
    By transitivity of $\mathcal{U}_i$, $\ensuremath{\llbracket T[q(\sigma)] \rrbracket((\rho, a/x))} \approx
    \ensuremath{\llbracket T \rrbracket((\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\rho)}, a'/x))} \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_I)$.
  \end{itemize}
  By \textsc{U-Pi} with this domain and codomain:
  \[
    \Pi(\ensuremath{\llbracket S[\sigma] \rrbracket(\rho)},\, T[q(\sigma)],\, \rho)
    \approx \Pi(\ensuremath{\llbracket S \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\rho)})},\, T,\, \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\rho)})
    \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R.
  \]
  This is the outer-left $\approx$ inner-left cross-relation.
  By symmetry and transitivity of $\mathcal{U}_i$ combined with the outer-pair and
  inner-pair relations, all six pairs among the four $\Pi$-values are related in
  $\mathcal{U}_i \searrow R$.

  Hence all four $\Pi$-values lie pairwise in $\mathcal{U}_i \searrow R$.
