title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\Gamma' \approx \Gamma' \searrow R'$,
  $\semtyeq[\Gamma']{\sigma}{\sigma'}{\Gamma}$, and
  $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}} :: \rho \approx \rho' \in R'$ be given.

  \emph{Type part.}
  By \Cref{lem:fund-pi-wf} applied to the hypotheses $\semtyeq[\Gamma]{S}{S}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}$
  and $\semtyeq[\Gamma, x:S]{T}{T}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}$ (the latter follows from
  $\semtyeq[\Gamma, x:S]{t}{t}{T}$ via type extraction):
  \[
    \{\ensuremath{\llbracket (\Pi(x:S).\,T)[\sigma] \rrbracket(\rho)},\;
    \ensuremath{\llbracket \Pi(x:S).\,T \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\rho)})},\;
    \ensuremath{\llbracket \Pi(x:S).\,T \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma' \rrbracket(\rho')})},\;
    \ensuremath{\llbracket (\Pi(x:S).\,T)[\sigma'] \rrbracket(\rho')}\}
    \subseteq \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R
  \]
  where $R$ is the function PER characterized by:
  $f \approx f' \in R \;\leftrightarrow\;
  (\forall \ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_I :: a \approx a' \in R_I.\; f \cdot a \approx f' \cdot a' \in R_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_I))$.

  \emph{Term part.}
  We compute the four term values using the substitution behavior of $\lambda$:
  \begin{align*}
    &\ensuremath{\llbracket (\lambda x.\,t)[\sigma] \rrbracket(\rho)}
      = \ensuremath{\llbracket \lambda x.\,(t[q(\sigma)]) \rrbracket(\rho)}
      && \text{(by definition of substitution under $\lambda$)} \\
    &\quad = \lambda(t[q(\sigma)],\, \rho)
      && \text{(by evaluation of $\lambda$, forming a closure)} \\[4pt]
    &\ensuremath{\llbracket \lambda x.\,t \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\rho)})}
      = \lambda(t,\, \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\rho)})
      && \text{(by evaluation of $\lambda$)}
  \end{align*}
  Analogously, $\ensuremath{\llbracket \lambda x.\,t' \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma' \rrbracket(\rho')})} = \lambda(t',\, \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma' \rrbracket(\rho')})$
  and $\ensuremath{\llbracket (\lambda x.\,t')[\sigma'] \rrbracket(\rho')} = \lambda(t'[q(\sigma')],\, \rho')$.

  By the biconditional characterization of $R$, it suffices to show that for every
  $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_I :: a \approx a' \in R_I$ (where $R_I$ is the domain PER), the four closure
  applications are related in $R_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_I)$:
  \[
    \{\lambda(t[q(\sigma)], \rho) \cdot a,\;
    \lambda(t, \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\rho)}) \cdot a,\;
    \lambda(t', \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma' \rrbracket(\rho')}) \cdot a',\;
    \lambda(t'[q(\sigma')], \rho') \cdot a'\}
    \subseteq R_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_I).
  \]

  We compute these closure applications:
  \begin{align*}
    &\lambda(t[q(\sigma)],\, \rho) \cdot a
      = \ensuremath{\llbracket t[q(\sigma)] \rrbracket((\rho, a/x))}
      && \text{(by closure application)} \\
    &\lambda(t,\, \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\rho)}) \cdot a
      = \ensuremath{\llbracket t \rrbracket((\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\rho)}, a/x))}
      && \text{(by closure application)}
  \end{align*}
  Analogous identities hold for the primed pair (using $t'$).

  By \Cref{lem:sem-q} on $\semtyeq[\Gamma']{\sigma}{\sigma'}{\Gamma}$ and
  $\semtyeq[\Gamma]{S}{S}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}$:
  $\semtyeq[\Gamma', x:S[\sigma]]{q(\sigma)}{q(\sigma')}{\Gamma, x:S}$.
  By the first premise of this judgment,
  $(\Gamma', x:S[\sigma]) \approx (\Gamma', x:S[\sigma]) \searrow R_{\Gamma',x:S[\sigma]}$
  and $(\Gamma, x:S) \approx (\Gamma, x:S) \searrow R_{\Gamma,x:S}$.

  By \Cref{lem:univ-functional} on the same left type $\ensuremath{\llbracket S[\sigma] \rrbracket(\rho)}$
  governing both $R_I$ (from \Cref{lem:fund-pi-wf}'s domain step) and the head PER
  $R_H'$ of $R_{\Gamma',x:S[\sigma]}$, $R_I \Leftrightarrow R_H'(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}')$ for
  $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}' :: \rho \approx \rho' \in R'$.
  Hence $a \approx a' \in R_H'(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}')$, so by the biconditional of
  $R_{\Gamma',x:S[\sigma]}$,
  $(\rho, a/x) \approx (\rho', a'/x) \in R_{\Gamma',x:S[\sigma]}$.

  Apply the hypothesis $\semtyeq[\Gamma, x:S]{t}{t'}{T}$ at $\Gamma', x:S[\sigma]$,
  the lifted substitution
  $\semtyeq[\Gamma', x:S[\sigma]]{q(\sigma)}{q(\sigma')}{\Gamma, x:S}$, and
  $(\rho, a/x) \approx (\rho', a'/x) \in R_{\Gamma',x:S[\sigma]}$:
  \begin{align*}
    &\{\ensuremath{\llbracket t[q(\sigma)] \rrbracket((\rho, a/x))},\;
      \ensuremath{\llbracket t \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket q(\sigma) \rrbracket((\rho, a/x))})},\\
    &\quad \ensuremath{\llbracket t' \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket q(\sigma') \rrbracket((\rho', a'/x))})},\;
      \ensuremath{\llbracket t'[q(\sigma')] \rrbracket((\rho', a'/x))}\}
      \subseteq R_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_I)
      && \text{(by hypothesis on $t, t'$)}
  \end{align*}
  The outer two values are the closure applications
  $\lambda(t[q(\sigma)], \rho) \cdot a$ and $\lambda(t'[q(\sigma')], \rho') \cdot a'$.
  The inner two values are $\ensuremath{\llbracket t \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket q(\sigma) \rrbracket((\rho, a/x))})}$ and
  $\ensuremath{\llbracket t' \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket q(\sigma') \rrbracket((\rho', a'/x))})}$, which we must relate to
  $\ensuremath{\llbracket t \rrbracket((\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\rho)}, a/x))} = \lambda(t, \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\rho)}) \cdot a$
  and $\ensuremath{\llbracket t' \rrbracket((\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma' \rrbracket(\rho')}, a'/x))} = \lambda(t', \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma' \rrbracket(\rho')}) \cdot a'$.

  We now show
  $\ensuremath{\llbracket q(\sigma) \rrbracket((\rho, a/x))} \approx (\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\rho)}, a/x) \in R_{\Gamma, x:S}$.
  Unfolding $q(\sigma) = (\sigma[\Uparrow], x_0/x)$, the environment
  $\ensuremath{\llbracket q(\sigma) \rrbracket((\rho, a/x))}$ has tail $\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma[\Uparrow] \rrbracket((\rho, a/x))}$ and
  head $a$ (since $\ensuremath{\llbracket x_0 \rrbracket((\rho, a/x))} = a$).
  The environment $(\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\rho)}, a/x)$ has tail $\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\rho)}$ and
  head $a$.
  By the biconditional of $R_{\Gamma, x:S}$ (from \textsc{Ctx-Ext}), it suffices to
  show:
  \begin{itemize}
  \@idxitem \emph{Tails:}
    $\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma[\Uparrow] \rrbracket((\rho, a/x))} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\rho)} \in R_\Gamma$.
    By \Cref{lem:sem-wk-shift}, $\semweak[\Gamma',x:S[\sigma]]{\Uparrow}{\Gamma'}$.
    Apply $\semtyeq[\Gamma']{\sigma}{\sigma'}{\Gamma}$ at $\Gamma', x:S[\sigma]$,
    $\Uparrow$, and $(\rho, a/x) \approx (\rho', a'/x) \in R_{\Gamma',x:S[\sigma]}$:
    the four-value pattern includes
    $\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma[\Uparrow] \rrbracket((\rho, a/x))} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \Uparrow \rrbracket((\rho, a/x))})} \in R_\Gamma$.
    Since $\ensuremath{\llbracket \Uparrow \rrbracket((\rho, a/x))} = \rho$ definitionally (the shift on
    environments drops the head), this gives the desired relatedness.
    Let $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_\Gamma$ denote this evidence in $R_\Gamma$.
  \@idxitem \emph{Heads:}
    $a \approx a \in R_H^\Gamma(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_\Gamma)$, where $R_H^\Gamma(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_\Gamma)$ is the
    head PER governed by
    $\ensuremath{\llbracket S \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma[\Uparrow] \rrbracket((\rho, a/x))})} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket S \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\rho)})}
    \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_H^\Gamma(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_\Gamma)$.
    By $\semtyeq[\Gamma]{S}{S}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}$ instantiated at $\Gamma'$,
    $\semtyeq[\Gamma']{\sigma}{\sigma}{\Gamma}$ (reflexive, by
    \Cref{lem:sem-sym,lem:sem-trans}), and $\rho \approx \rho \in R'$: the type part
    gives the commutation
    $\ensuremath{\llbracket S[\sigma] \rrbracket(\rho)} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket S \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\rho)})} \in \mathcal{U}_i$.
    By \Cref{lem:univ-functional}, $R_I \Leftrightarrow R_H^\Gamma(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_\Gamma)$.
    From $a \approx a \in R_I$ (reflexive of $a \approx a' \in R_I$), we conclude
    $a \approx a \in R_H^\Gamma(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_\Gamma)$.
  \end{itemize}
  By \textsc{Ctx-Ext}'s biconditional,
  $\ensuremath{\llbracket q(\sigma) \rrbracket((\rho, a/x))} \approx (\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\rho)}, a/x) \in R_{\Gamma, x:S}$.
  By \Cref{lem:sem-ty-id} on the reflexive instance
  $\semtyeq[\Gamma, x:S]{t}{t}{T}$ (from $\semtyeq[\Gamma, x:S]{t}{t'}{T}$ by
  \Cref{lem:sem-sym,lem:sem-trans}) applied to this related pair:
  \[
    \ensuremath{\llbracket t \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket q(\sigma) \rrbracket((\rho, a/x))})} \approx
    \ensuremath{\llbracket t \rrbracket((\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\rho)}, a/x))} \in R_O'(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_I)
  \]
  for some $R_O'(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_I)$.
  By \Cref{lem:univ-functional}, $R_O'(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_I) \Leftrightarrow R_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_I)$
  (governed by the same type $\ensuremath{\llbracket T \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket q(\sigma) \rrbracket((\rho, a/x))})}$ which lies in
  $\mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_I)$ by the type part of the four-value pattern).
  Analogously on the primed side (using the reflexive instance $\semtyeq[\Gamma, x:S]{t'}{t'}{T}$):
  $\ensuremath{\llbracket t' \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket q(\sigma') \rrbracket((\rho', a'/x))})} \approx
  \ensuremath{\llbracket t' \rrbracket((\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma' \rrbracket(\rho')}, a'/x))} \in R_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_I)$.

  Combining via symmetry and transitivity of $R_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_I)$, the four closure
  applications
  \[
    \{\lambda(t[q(\sigma)], \rho) \cdot a,\;
    \lambda(t, \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\rho)}) \cdot a,\;
    \lambda(t', \ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma' \rrbracket(\rho')}) \cdot a',\;
    \lambda(t'[q(\sigma')], \rho') \cdot a'\}
    \subseteq R_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_I).
  \]
  Hence the biconditional is satisfied, and the four closures are related in $R$.

title: Proof
body_md:
By the fundamental theorem (\Cref{thm:fundamental}, statement (3)):
  $\semtyeq[\Gamma]{s}{t}{T}$.
  Unfolding, this means: for all $\Gamma' \approx \Gamma' \searrow R'$, all
  $\semtyeq[\Gamma']{\sigma}{\sigma'}{\Gamma}$, all $\rho \approx \rho' \in R'$,
  the evaluations of $s$ and $t$ are related in the appropriate PER.

  We instantiate at:
  \begin{itemize}
  \@idxitem $\Gamma' := \Gamma$ (by statement (1), $\Gamma \approx \Gamma \searrow R$ for some $R$),
  \@idxitem $\sigma := \sigma' := \ensuremath{\textsf{id}}$ (the identity substitution is semantic by \Cref{lem:sem-id}),
  \@idxitem $\rho := \rho' := {\uparrow}^\Gamma$ (the initial environment is in $R$ by \Cref{lem:init-in-per}).
  \end{itemize}
  Since $s[\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}] = s$ and $t[\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}] = t$, and $\ensuremath{\llbracket \ensuremath{\textsf{id}} \rrbracket(\rho)} = \rho$, we obtain:
  \begin{align*}
    &\ensuremath{\llbracket T \rrbracket({\uparrow}^\Gamma)} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket T \rrbracket({\uparrow}^\Gamma)}
      \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_T
      && \text{(type part, with LHS = RHS since $\sigma = \sigma'$ and $\rho = \rho'$)} \\
    &\ensuremath{\llbracket s \rrbracket({\uparrow}^\Gamma)} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket t \rrbracket({\uparrow}^\Gamma)} \in R_T
      && \text{(term part)}
  \end{align*}

  Let $A = \ensuremath{\llbracket T \rrbracket({\uparrow}^\Gamma)}$, $a = \ensuremath{\llbracket s \rrbracket({\uparrow}^\Gamma)}$, and
  $b = \ensuremath{\llbracket t \rrbracket({\uparrow}^\Gamma)}$.
  Then $A \approx A \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_T$ and $a \approx b \in R_T$.

  By realizability (\Cref{lem:R-readback}):
  ${\downarrow}^A(a) \approx {\downarrow}^A(b) \in \textsf{Nf}$.
  Unfolding the definition of $\textsf{Nf}$: for all $n$, there exists $w$ such that
  $\textsf{R}^{\textsf{Nf}}_n({\downarrow}^A(a)) \searrow w$ and $\textsf{R}^{\textsf{Nf}}_n({\downarrow}^A(b)) \searrow w$.

  Taking $n = |\Gamma|$ (the length of $\Gamma$, which provides enough fresh names):
  \begin{align*}
    &\textsf{nbe}_\Gamma^T(s)
      = \textsf{R}^{\textsf{Nf}}_{|\Gamma|}({\downarrow}^{\ensuremath{\llbracket T \rrbracket({\uparrow}^\Gamma)}}(\ensuremath{\llbracket s \rrbracket({\uparrow}^\Gamma)}))
      = \textsf{R}^{\textsf{Nf}}_{|\Gamma|}({\downarrow}^A(a))
      \searrow w \\
    &\textsf{nbe}_\Gamma^T(t)
      = \textsf{R}^{\textsf{Nf}}_{|\Gamma|}({\downarrow}^{\ensuremath{\llbracket T \rrbracket({\uparrow}^\Gamma)}}(\ensuremath{\llbracket t \rrbracket({\uparrow}^\Gamma)}))
      = \textsf{R}^{\textsf{Nf}}_{|\Gamma|}({\downarrow}^A(b))
      \searrow w
  \end{align*}
  Hence $\textsf{nbe}_\Gamma^T(s) = w = \textsf{nbe}_\Gamma^T(t)$.

  We write $\Vdash \Gamma$ to mean that the context-gluing predicate exists
  for $\Gamma$:
  \[

body_md:
By $\Vdash \Gamma$, fix $\Gamma \searrow \textsf{Sb}_T$ for some $\textsf{Sb}_T$.

  \emph{Syntactic typing of $S$.}
  By \Cref{lem:init-env-valid} on $\Gamma \searrow \textsf{Sb}_T$, the initial
  pair $\judge[\Gamma]{\ensuremath{\textsf{id}} : \Gamma} \;\circledR\; {\uparrow}^\Gamma \in \textsf{Sb}_T$

  $\typing[\Gamma]{S[\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}]}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} \;\circledR\; P$ for some $P$, hence
  $\typing[\Gamma]{S}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}$ by \Cref{lem:gluing-typ-escape} (using
  $S[\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}] = S$).

  \emph{Universal type-clause.}
  Let $\judge[\Delta']{\sigma_T : \Gamma} \;\circledR\; \rho_T \in \textsf{Sb}_T$
  be arbitrary. By $\Semtyp[\Gamma]{S}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}$ at $\sigma_T, \rho_T$:
  \begin{align*}
    &\ensuremath{\llbracket S \rrbracket(\rho_T)} \searrow a,\;
      a \in \mathcal{U}_i^\ast \searrow P \searrow \textbf{El}
      && \text{(by $\Semtyp[\Gamma]{S}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}$ at $\sigma_T, \rho_T$)} \\
    &\typing[\Delta']{S[\sigma_T]}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} \;\circledR\; P
      && \text{(by $\Semtyp[\Gamma]{S}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}$, type part)}
  \end{align*}
  This supplies the universal-clause witness for the given
  $\sigma_T, \rho_T$.

  By \textsc{G-Ctx-Ext}: $(\Gamma, x:S) \searrow \textsf{Sb}$ where
  $\textsf{Sb} \Leftrightarrow \textsf{Cons}_i(\Gamma, S, \textsf{Sb}_T)$.
  Hence $\Vdash \Gamma, x:S$ by \Cref{def:sound-semctx}.

title: Proof
body_md:
$\Vdash \Gamma$ is presupposed by the hypothesis $\Semtyp[\Gamma]{t}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Nat}}}$.
  Fix $\Gamma \searrow \textsf{Sb}$ and let
  $\judge[\Delta]{\sigma : \Gamma} \;\circledR\; \rho \in \textsf{Sb}$ be given.
  We establish the four clauses of $\Semtyp[\Gamma]{\textsf{succ}~t}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Nat}}}$ at
  $a = N$, $P = \textsf{Nat}_i$, $\textbf{El} = \textsf{Nat}_i$.
  \begin{align*}
    &\ensuremath{\llbracket \ensuremath{\texttt{Nat}} \rrbracket(\rho)} \searrow N
      && \text{(by \textsc{ev-N})} \tag*{[clause 1]} \\
    &N \in \mathcal{U}_i^\ast \searrow \textsf{Nat}_i \searrow \textsf{Nat}_i
      && \text{(by \textsc{G-Nat})} \tag*{[clause 2]} \\
    &\typing[\Delta]{\ensuremath{\texttt{Nat}}[\sigma]}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} \;\circledR\; \textsf{Nat}_i
      && \text{(by \Cref{def:nat-type-pred} with $\ensuremath{\texttt{Nat}}[\sigma] = \ensuremath{\texttt{Nat}}$)}
      \tag*{[clause 3]} \\
    &\ensuremath{\llbracket t \rrbracket(\rho)} \searrow b
      && \text{(by hypothesis on $t$)} \\
    &\typing[\Delta]{t[\sigma]}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Nat}}[\sigma]} \;\circledR\;
      b \in \textsf{Nat}_i
      && \text{(by hypothesis on $t$, term part)} \\
    &\ensuremath{\llbracket \textsf{succ}~t \rrbracket(\rho)} \searrow \texttt{su}(b)
      && \text{(by \textsc{ev-su})} \\
    &(\textsf{succ}~t)[\sigma] = \textsf{succ}~t[\sigma]
      && \text{(syntactic substitution on $\textsf{succ}~$)} \\
    &\typing[\Delta]{(\textsf{succ}~t)[\sigma]}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Nat}}[\sigma]} \;\circledR\;
      \texttt{su}(b) \in \textsf{Nat}_i
      && \text{(by \textsc{GN-Su} combined with the type predicate above,}\\
    & && \text{\Cref{def:nat-term-pred})} \tag*{[clause 4]}
  \end{align*}

title: Proof
body_md:
$\Vdash \Gamma$ and $\Vdash \Gamma, x:S_1$ are presupposed.
  Fix $\Gamma \searrow \textsf{Sb}_\Gamma$ and
  $(\Gamma, x:S_1) \searrow \textsf{Sb}_{\Gamma,x:S_1}$ where
  $\textsf{Sb}_{\Gamma,x:S_1} \Leftrightarrow
  \textsf{Cons}_i(\Gamma, S_1, \textsf{Sb}_\Gamma)$ by \textsc{G-Ctx-Ext}.
  Let $\judge[\Delta]{\sigma : \Gamma} \;\circledR\; \rho \in
  \textsf{Sb}_\Gamma$ be given.

  \emph{Unpacking the hypotheses.}
  \begin{align*}
    &\ensuremath{\llbracket r \rrbracket(\rho)} \searrow f
      && \text{(by hypothesis on $r$, evaluation clause)} \\
    &\typing[\Delta]{r[\sigma]}{(\Pi(x:S_1).\,S_2)[\sigma]} \;\circledR\;
      f \in \Pi_i^{\textbf{El}}(R, R_I, P_I, \textbf{El}_I, \textbf{El}_O)
      && \text{(by hypothesis on $r$, term clause)} \\
    &\ensuremath{\llbracket s \rrbracket(\rho)} \searrow b
      && \text{(by hypothesis on $s$, evaluation clause)} \\
    &\typing[\Delta]{s[\sigma]}{S_1[\sigma]} \;\circledR\; b \in \textbf{El}_I
      && \text{(by hypothesis on $s$, term clause)} \\
    &b \approx b \in R_I
      && \text{(by \Cref{lem:gluing-implies-per})}
  \end{align*}
  Let $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}} :: b \approx b \in R_I$. Here $P_O, \textbf{El}_O$ are functions of
  $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}$, supplied by the $\Pi$-gluing of $f$.

  \emph{Building the substitution-environment pair for $S_2$.} Set
  $\sigma_* := (\sigma,\, s[\sigma]/x)$.
  \begin{align*}
    &\judge[\Delta]{\sigma_* : \Gamma, x:S_1}
      \;\circledR\; (\rho, b/x) \in \textsf{Sb}_{\Gamma,x:S_1}
      && \text{(by $\textsf{Cons}_i$ on $\sigma, \rho \in
        \textsf{Sb}_\Gamma$ and the term} \\
    & && \text{gluing of $s[\sigma]$, taking the trailing weakening
        as $\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}$)}
  \end{align*}

  \emph{Instantiating the codomain semantic typing.} Apply
  $\Semtyp[\Gamma, x:S_1]{S_2}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}$ at $\sigma_*, (\rho, b/x)$:
  \begin{align*}
    &\ensuremath{\llbracket S_2 \rrbracket((\rho, b/x))} \searrow a_2
      && \text{(by hypothesis on $S_2$, evaluation clause)} \\
    &a_2 \in \mathcal{U}_i^\ast \searrow P_2 \searrow \textbf{El}_2
      && \text{(by hypothesis on $S_2$, gluing clause)} \\
    &\typing[\Delta]{S_2[\sigma_*]}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} \;\circledR\; P_2
      && \text{(by hypothesis on $S_2$, type clause)}
  \end{align*}

  \emph{Reconciling $(P_2, \textbf{El}_2)$ with $(P_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}), \textbf{El}_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}))$.} The
  $\Pi$-gluing of $f$, by \textsc{G-Pi}, requires
  $\ensuremath{\llbracket S_2 \rrbracket((\rho, b/x))} \searrow c$ implies $c \in \mathcal{U}_i^\ast \searrow
  P_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}) \searrow \textbf{El}_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}})$. By determinism, $c = a_2$, so
  $a_2 \in \mathcal{U}_i^\ast \searrow P_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}) \searrow \textbf{El}_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}})$.
  By \Cref{lem:gluing-functional}, gluing-model predicates at a fixed
  domain value are unique up to logical equivalence:
  \begin{align*}
    &P_2 \Leftrightarrow P_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}),\quad
      \textbf{El}_2 \Leftrightarrow \textbf{El}_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}})
      && \text{(by \Cref{lem:gluing-functional})}
  \end{align*}

  \emph{Application via the $\Pi$-gluing of $f$.} Instantiate the
  application clause (\Cref{def:pi-term-pred} clause~(4)) on $f$ at the
  identity Kripke weakening $\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}$, term $s[\sigma]$,
  value $b$, witness $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}$:
  \begin{align*}
    &f \cdot b \searrow c
      && \text{(by clause (4) on $f$)} \\
    &\typing[\Delta]{(r[\sigma][\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}])\;s[\sigma]}
      {S_2[\iota(\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}) \circ q(\sigma),\, s[\sigma]/x]}
      \;\circledR\; c \in \textbf{El}_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}})
      && \text{(by clause (4) on $f$)} \\
    &r[\sigma][\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}] = r[\sigma]
      && \text{(by \Cref{lem:subst-id})} \\
    &\iota(\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}) = \ensuremath{\textsf{id}}
      && \text{(by definition of $\iota$ on the identity weakening)} \\
    &S_2[\iota(\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}) \circ q(\sigma),\, s[\sigma]/x] = S_2[\sigma_*]
      && \text{(via \Cref{lem:q-ext} and identity absorption)} \\
    &\typing[\Delta]{(r[\sigma])\;s[\sigma]}{S_2[\sigma_*]}
      \;\circledR\; c \in \textbf{El}_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}})
      && \text{(rewriting the previous gluing line)}
  \end{align*}

  \emph{Type rewriting from $S_2[\sigma_*]$ to $S_2[s/x][\sigma]$.}
  \begin{align*}
    &S_2[\sigma_*] = S_2[(\sigma, s[\sigma]/x)] = S_2[q(\sigma)][s[\sigma]/x]
      && \text{(by \Cref{lem:q-ext})} \\
    &S_2[s/x][\sigma] = S_2[\sigma, s[\sigma]/x] = S_2[\sigma_*]
      && \text{(by \Cref{lem:subst-ext-comm})}
  \end{align*}

  \emph{Bridging $\ensuremath{\llbracket S_2[s/x] \rrbracket(\rho)}$ to $a_2$.} With operational
  substitutions, $\ensuremath{\llbracket S_2[s/x] \rrbracket(\rho)}$ does not directly evaluate to
  $a_2$. By \Cref{thm:fundamental} of \Cref{sec:comp} on
  $\typing[\Gamma, x:S_1]{S_2}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}$ (escaped from the $S_2$
  hypothesis), we obtain $\semtyeq[\Gamma, x:S_1]{S_2}{S_2}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}$. By
  \Cref{thm:fundamental} on the substitution typing
  $\judge[\Gamma]{(\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}, s/x) : \Gamma, x:S_1}$ (derivable from
  $\typing[\Gamma]{s}{S_1}$ via the substitution-extension rule), we
  obtain $\semtyeq[\Gamma]{(\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}, s/x)}{(\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}, s/x)}{\Gamma, x:S_1}$.
  Instantiate $\semtyeq[\Gamma, x:S_1]{S_2}{S_2}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}$ at outer context
  $\Gamma$, this semantic substitution, and $\rho \approx \rho \in
  \ensuremath{\llbracket \Gamma \rrbracket}$ (the latter from $\rho \in \textsf{Sb}_\Gamma$ via
  \Cref{lem:gluing-implies-per}). The four-value pattern of
  \Cref{def:sem-term-eq} yields:
  \begin{align*}
    &\ensuremath{\llbracket (\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}, s/x) \rrbracket(\rho)} \searrow (\rho, b/x)
      && \text{(by \textsc{ev-ext} on $\ensuremath{\llbracket \ensuremath{\textsf{id}} \rrbracket(\rho)} \searrow \rho$
        and $\ensuremath{\llbracket s \rrbracket(\rho)} \searrow b$)} \\
    &\ensuremath{\llbracket S_2[(\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}, s/x)] \rrbracket(\rho)} \searrow a_2'
      && \text{(by the four-value pattern, outer left value)} \\
    &S_2[s/x] = S_2[(\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}, s/x)]
      && \text{(by definition: single-substitution sugar)} \\
    &\ensuremath{\llbracket S_2[s/x] \rrbracket(\rho)} \searrow a_2'
      && \text{(rewriting)} \\
    &a_2' \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket S_2 \rrbracket((\rho, b/x))} \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}})
      && \text{(by the four-value pattern, outer-inner relatedness)} \\
    &a_2' \approx a_2 \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}})
      && \text{(by determinism: $\ensuremath{\llbracket S_2 \rrbracket((\rho, b/x))} = a_2$)} \\
    &a_2' \in \mathcal{U}_i^\ast \searrow P_2 \searrow \textbf{El}_2
      && \text{(by \Cref{lem:gluing-univ-equiv} symmetric form on
        $a_2 \in \mathcal{U}_i^\ast$)}
  \end{align*}

  \emph{Assembling the four clauses of $\Semtyp[\Gamma]{r\;s}{S_2[s/x]}$.}
  At $a := a_2'$, $P := P_2$, $\textbf{El} := \textbf{El}_2$:
  \begin{align*}
    &\ensuremath{\llbracket S_2[s/x] \rrbracket(\rho)} \searrow a_2'
      && \tag*{[clause 1]} \\
    &a_2' \in \mathcal{U}_i^\ast \searrow P_2 \searrow \textbf{El}_2
      && \tag*{[clause 2]} \\
    &\typing[\Delta]{S_2[s/x][\sigma]}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} \;\circledR\; P_2
      && \text{(rewriting $S_2[\sigma_*] = S_2[s/x][\sigma]$ on the
        type-clause line)} \tag*{[clause 3]} \\
    &\ensuremath{\llbracket r\;s \rrbracket(\rho)} \searrow c
      && \text{(by \textsc{ev-app} on $\ensuremath{\llbracket r \rrbracket(\rho)} \searrow f$,
        $\ensuremath{\llbracket s \rrbracket(\rho)} \searrow b$, $f \cdot b \searrow c$)} \\
    &(r\;s)[\sigma] = r[\sigma]\;s[\sigma]
      && \text{(by syntactic substitution on application)} \\
    &\typing[\Delta]{r\;s[\sigma]}{S_2[\sigma_*]}
      \;\circledR\; c \in \textbf{El}_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}})
      && \text{(established above)} \\
    &\typing[\Delta]{(r\;s)[\sigma]}{S_2[s/x][\sigma]}
      \;\circledR\; c \in \textbf{El}_2
      && \text{(rewriting via $S_2[\sigma_*] = S_2[s/x][\sigma]$
        and $\textbf{El}_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}) \Leftrightarrow \textbf{El}_2$)} \tag*{[clause 4]}
  \end{align*}

  $\judge[\Delta]{\sigma : \Gamma} \;\circledR\; \rho \in \textsf{Sb}$ be given.

  \begin{align*}
    &\ensuremath{\llbracket S \rrbracket(\rho)} \searrow a_S,\;
      a_S \in \mathcal{U}_i^\ast \searrow P_S \searrow \textbf{El}_S
      && \text{(by hypothesis on $t$, evaluation and gluing clauses)} \\
    &\ensuremath{\llbracket T \rrbracket(\rho)} \searrow a_T,\;
      a_T \in \mathcal{U}_i^\ast \searrow P_T \searrow \textbf{El}_T
      && \text{(by hypothesis on $T$, evaluation and gluing clauses)} \\
    &\typing[\Delta]{t[\sigma]}{S[\sigma]} \;\circledR\;
      \ensuremath{\llbracket t \rrbracket(\rho)} \in \textbf{El}_S
      && \text{(by hypothesis on $t$, term clause)} \\
    &\rho \approx \rho \in R_\Gamma
      && \text{(by \Cref{lem:gluing-implies-per} on
        $\rho \in \textsf{Sb}$)} \\
    &\semtyeq[\Gamma]{\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}}{\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}}{\Gamma}
      && \text{(by \Cref{lem:sem-id})} \\
    &a_S \mathrel{<:_i} a_T
      && \text{(by $\Gamma \vDash S \subseteq T$ instantiated at} \\
    & && \text{the identity semantic substitution and
        $\rho \approx \rho$:} \\
    & && \text{the inner-pair relation gives
        $\ensuremath{\llbracket S \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \ensuremath{\textsf{id}} \rrbracket(\rho)})} \mathrel{<:_i}
        \ensuremath{\llbracket T \rrbracket(\ensuremath{\llbracket \ensuremath{\textsf{id}} \rrbracket(\rho)})}$,} \\
    & && \text{which is $\ensuremath{\llbracket S \rrbracket(\rho)} \mathrel{<:_i}
        \ensuremath{\llbracket T \rrbracket(\rho)}$)} \\
    &\typing[\Delta]{T[\sigma]}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} \;\circledR\; P_T
      && \text{(by hypothesis on $T$, type clause)} \\
    &\typing[\Delta]{t[\sigma]}{T[\sigma]} \;\circledR\;
      \ensuremath{\llbracket t \rrbracket(\rho)} \in \textbf{El}_T
      && \text{(by \Cref{lem:gluing-subty} on $a_S \mathrel{<:_i} a_T$,
        $a_S \in \textbf{El}_S$,} \\
    & && \text{and $T[\sigma] \;\circledR\; P_T$)}
  \end{align*}

body_md:
By soundness, $\tyequiv[\Gamma]{s}{\textsf{nbe}_\Gamma^T(s)}{T}$ and
  $\tyequiv[\Gamma]{t}{\textsf{nbe}_\Gamma^T(t)}{T}$.
  By completeness, $\tyequiv[\Gamma]{s}{t}{T}$ iff
  $\textsf{nbe}_\Gamma^T(s) = \textsf{nbe}_\Gamma^T(t)$.
  Comparing normal forms is decidable.
